We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
The Senior Clinical Data Scientist will be part of the Ion business unit.  The Ion endoluminal system is Intuitive's robotic platform for minimally invasive biopsy in the peripheral lung, with an initial goal of improving the early diagnosis of lung cancer. The Senior Clinical Data Scientist sits at the intersection of clinical science and data science within the Ion business unit, translating clinical questions into rigorous, data-driven analyses that inform product strategy, evidence generation, and business decisions. This role reports to the Managing Staff, Clinical Data Science.
The individual in this role will partner with clinicians, cross-functional teams, and data engineering to design and execute a clinical data science strategy — defining hypotheses grounded in customer needs, identifying appropriate data sources, conducting quantitative analyses, and communicating results that demonstrably impact patient outcomes and business objectives. Unlike a purely clinical or purely technical role, this position demands both deep clinical understanding of the Ion platform and hands-on proficiency in modern data science methods and tools.
Success requires a strong technical foundation in Python or R, statistics, and causal reasoning; the ability to navigate ambiguity in a fast-evolving clinical and commercial landscape; and exceptional skill in communicating complex findings clearly — especially through polished visual presentations and well-organized documentation.
Essential Job Duties
Work with internal and external stakeholders (including clinicians, administrators, and policymakers) to identify data-centric needs in the clinical space and translate them into prioritized research questions with testable hypotheses.
Design, implement, and validate quantitative analyses in Python or R — applying appropriate statistical, machine learning, and causal inference methods to Ion device logs, clinical studies/registries, insurance claims databases, and EHR/EMR data — to test hypotheses.
Translate analyses into decision-useful stories, tailoring them to diverse groups of stakeholders — from technical peers building product, to senior leadership defining strategy, to external physicians looking to improve efficiency.
Demonstrate impact through internal/external reports, presentations, dashboards, peer-reviewed publications, and customer-facing deliverables.
Partner with cross-functional teams to assist with the design and execution of global clinical and economic evidence strategies, including designing and supporting clinical trials.
Support regulatory submissions by structuring and validating clinical datasets to meet FDA and EU MDR compliance standards.
Create and maintain well-organized, reproducible codebases with clear documentation, version control, and consistent coding standards.
Catalyze a data-driven culture internally — champion the use of data to generate compelling evidence and ultimately build a better product.
Required Skills and Experience
6+ years of experience with Master's degree or 4+ years with PhD in a quantitative, scientific, or engineering field (e.g., biostatistics, epidemiology, data science, computer science, biomedical engineering, public health, or a related discipline). MD with quantitative research experience also accepted.
Experience with Python or R for data analysis, statistical modeling, and visualization.
Working knowledge of SQL for querying and managing structured datasets.
Demonstrated experience with causal inference methods and study design.
Experience working with device-generated log data, clinical study/registry data, and claims/EHR-style databases.
Experience with causal inference in a healthcare or medical device context.
Experience using platforms such as Snowflake or Databricks for production-level data pipelines and analytics.
Experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau) for the presentation of complex data to non-technical stakeholders or regulatory bodies.
Experience with Electronic Data Capture (EDC) systems (e.g., Medrio) for managing clinical study/registry data.
Experience using AI/ML tools to accelerate software development and data analysis workflows.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Excellent critical thinking and analytical skills, with the ability to frame ambiguous clinical questions as testable hypotheses and select fit-for-purpose methods.
Stellar organizational skills, particularly with respect to code management and documentation.
Ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams, including clinicians, engineers, regulatory, commercial, and data science partners.
Self-starter attitude with the ability to manage multiple priorities, operate independently, and deliver under ambiguity.
Track record of peer-reviewed publications or conference presentations in clinical research or data science.
Experience in medical devices or other regulated industries.
Familiarity with Good Clinical Practice (GCP), ISO 14155 (clinical investigation of medical devices), and data privacy regulations (HIPAA/GDPR).
Familiarity with the lung cancer landscape (screening, diagnosis, treatment).

The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
The Future Forward organization is Intuitive’s advanced concepts group. We explore emerging technologies, prototype next-generation solutions, and build software experiences that shape the future of robotic-assisted surgery.
If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of the Position
This position requires a candidate with extensive experience helping evidence generation strategy and execution of clinical studies. The Clinical Study Manager-4 (CSM IV) role will develop and execute strategies for clinical and outcomes research studies to help regulatory approvals and key strategic evidence initiatives. As a member of the Clinical Affairs team, this role will be accountable for working with key stakeholders to design and develop clinical protocols and execute clinical studies (pre-market or post-market studies), with minimal supervision. The candidate will be required to work closely with clinical research associates (CRAs), clinical trial assistants (CTAs) and data management for the conduct and execution of the study, as well as with biostatisticians to review and interpret results of clinical studies, develop clinical study reports, or help the development of clinical publications. During trial execution, the CSM will drive the progress of the trial during site selection, site start-up and through enrollment and follow-up. The CSM will clearly provide guidance to the monitors about monitoring needs, and oversee compliance work on the study. The CSM will also take a leadership role in external communication with investigators and study teams. The ideal candidate will have experience previously managing premarket studies in the United States and utilizing resources to research and scope research topics and to provide recommendations on clinical trial strategy. The candidate is also expected to have experience reviewing, interpreting and summarizing clinical literature.
Essential Job Duties
Accountable for leading assigned clinical research activities
Partner with internal stakeholders, investigators and KOLs to develop and review study design and concepts, prepare protocol and study outlines and subsequently driving identified initiatives
Accountable for the planning and execution of the clinical studies including site selection, review of potential patient recruitment and projections, creation of study related documents (protocols, case report forms, Informed consents, Clinical trial agreements, study reports), organizing IRB/EC submissions with follow-thorough to ensure successful progress
Accountable for autonomously conducting clinical studies on schedule and within budget while ensuring high quality and compliance
Perform on-site and remote site qualification visits, site initiation visits, interim monitoring visits and site close out visits.
Conduct clinical study monitoring to ensure regulatory and protocol compliance as well as overall data accuracy in accordance with the study clinical monitoring plan
Complete source data verification of clinical study data entered in an Electronic Data Capture (EDC) system or on a case report form at sites or in data listings to ensure regulatory and protocol compliance and overall accuracy
Liaise with sites and help in internal audit/inspection and ensure sponsor audit readiness
Liaise with external vendors and sites to negotiate contracts and budgets in partnership with the legal team and management
Track study progress and provide regular status reports
Work closely with Biostatisticians on data analysis, interpretation and synthesis, in order to develop clinical study reports and /or help development of scientific publications
Track, process and manage site payments and help in study financial tracking by developing tracking tools as necessary
Organize and drive study meetings and other study activities as assigned
Mentor junior clinical study manager(s); provide guidance to CRAs and CTAs on monitoring and other study needs
Follow corporate (e.g., SOP’s) and regulatory requirements (e.g., GCP and US and OUS guidelines) and proactively manage studies, following such guidelines and requirements
Conduct literature searches and familiarize with literature to stay informed and abreast of relevant scientific/clinical knowledge and/or to establish evidence gaps
Critically appraise scientific literature and write clinical summaries to assist research and the development of clinical strategies and clinical investigational protocols
Review and revise Clinical Operations Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to assist Clinical Affairs leadership with continuous process improvement initiatives
For post-market research, partner with commercial groups (i.e., marketing) to know about market trends and utilize information to help of business goals through Clinical Affairs activities
For post-market research, provide scientific expertise to the Health Economics and Outcomes Research department for development of outcomes research review (including identification of appropriate diagnosis or reimbursement codes, selection of clinical outcomes for procedures of interest)
Work with clinical investigators to prepare manuscripts, abstracts, slide presentations, and poster presentations for scientific meetings and publications in partnership with management
Help regulatory submission and approval of pre-market clinical studies and 510k(s), accountable for addressing regulatory body questions on clinical study design and results (e.g., protocol, ICF, eCRF, clinical study reports).
Required Skills and Experience
Previous experience implementing, helping and managing medical device trials Significant knowledge of clinical and/or outcomes research study design
Proven experience in protocol and ICF development, writing clinical section(s) for regulatory submission
Proven experience in conducting literature searches, reviews and appraisal of the scientific data
Excellent ability to interact with physicians and other professionals inside and outside the company
Knowledge of Good Clinical Practice ICH/GCP and other applicable regulations, fundamental knowledge of clinical research and monitoring requirements
Experience negotiating clinical research contracts and budgets
Must be able to work effectively on cross-functional teams
Must be able to travel 25-40% or based on business requirements
Must be able to manage multiple projects and/or manage different priorities
Proven communication, presentation and relational skills with high attention to detail and organization
Ability to learn quickly, tailor to shifting requirements, and self-educate on different surgical specialties as applicable to clinical projects (“Self-starter attitude”)
Ability to drive project team consisting of CRAs and CTAs and support management with relevant study updates
Exhibits solid work ethic to help meet tight timelines or multiple projects when necessary with a problem-solving mindset
Required Education and Training
Minimum advanced degree in a scientific/bioengineering field (M.S., Ph.D. or M.D.) with a minimum of 5 years of experience in clinical research, or Bachelor’s degree in a scientific/bioengineering field with a minimum of 8 years of experience in clinical research is preferred, or a minimum of 10 years of experience in clinical research with relevant training.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Accustomed to working in a hospital environment, experience working with nurses and surgeons preferred
Knowledge of statistics, statistical methods, and design of experiment is highly preferred

description:

As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.

The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Position Summary
The Sr. Manager, Regulatory Affairs for the Digital Portfolio leads regulatory strategy and execution for software-driven products, including software as a medical device (SaMD), software in a medical device (SiMD), cloud and connected applications, data and analytics tools, and AI/ML-enabled features that support surgical care. This leader builds and manages a team of regulatory professionals and serves as the senior regulatory voice to Digital, R&D, Quality, Clinical, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Legal, and Commercial partners. The role ensures that digital innovations reach customers quickly, compliantly, and sustainably across global markets.
Key Responsibilities
Regulatory Strategy and Leadership
Develop and execute global regulatory strategies for digital products, aligned with business priorities and product roadmaps.
Determine device classification, qualification, and pathway for software functions, including whether features meet the definition of a medical device or fall under enforcement discretion.
Advise cross-functional leaders on regulatory risk, timelines, and trade-offs early in the design process.
Represent Regulatory Affairs on digital product core teams and governance forums.
Manage the regulatory assessment and ongoing oversight of the non-medical device portfolio of products, including determining non-device status, maintaining supporting rationale and documentation, and ensuring claims, labeling, and software updates do not change a product's regulatory status.
Submissions and Market Authorization
Lead preparation, review, and submission of 510(k), De Novo, and other premarket submissions.
Own regulatory strategy for software change management, including determining when changes require new submissions and leveraging Predetermined Change Control Plans (PCCPs) where appropriate.
Lead interactions with FDA including pre-submission meetings and responses to deficiency requests.
Software, AI/ML, and Cybersecurity Expertise

description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
We are looking for an experienced machine controls engineer to lead the development of advanced mechatronic instrumentation for patient care applications. The ideal candidate will have a proven track record of architecting and developing control and sensing software for medical robots or diagnostic instrumentation from prototype to commercialization. A strong skillset in experimental design, empirical data collection, and data analysis/visualization is critical. Experience in low-latency machine controls, high-precision optical control, and biological sample handling applications is highly desired. This position reports on-site at offices in the San Francisco Bay Area CA.
What You'll Do
Architect, design, and implement control and sensing software for advanced mechatronic instrumentation
Work hands-on with mechatronic hardware daily in system bring-up, calibration, operation, experimentation, and debugging
Lead system optimization and debugging activity with thoughtful experimental design, execution, and data analysis/visualization
Interface with embedded systems engineers and electrical engineers to develop appropriate software interfaces to lower-level controllers and firmware
Work closely with systems engineering and mechanical engineering to architect, select, and optimize electrical control boards, motors, sensors, and other hardware components
Write clean, structured and maintainable code, document software designs for various instrument configurations, inclusive of error recovery
Write and execute unit tests ensuring excellent test coverage for software code
Use scripting languages (e.g. Python) for bringing up various hardware prototypes, for test automation, and for data analysis/visualization
Generate detailed software requirements, design specifications, and software test protocols for the company’s Quality System
Work closely with a multidisciplinary engineering team and company leadership to deliver key technical milestones
Prioritize and debug reported software issues/bugs
Required Skills and Experience
BS/MS in Computer Science or related field with 8+ years industry experience, or PhD degree with 5+ years industry experience in systems control and sensing
Strong knowledge across programming languages for real-time and pseudo-real-time control (C#, C, C++) on Linux OS
Demonstrated experience in architecting and writing motion control, sensing, and state machine code for one or more diagnostic instruments or medical robots that have reached production
Experience in low-latency machine controls for time-sensitive applications
Strong experimental design, empirical data collection, and analysis/visualization skills to support design iteration and optimization using scripting languages such as Python
Experience developing medical device software per FDA requirements including software risk analysis and cybersecurity through all phases of product development lifecycle (design, implementation, debug, verification, validation and transfer to manufacturing)
Strong analytical skills and a creative mindset
Required Education and Training
• Bachelors, Master or PhD in Computer Science or related field
Preferred Skills and Experience
• Experience controlling high-speed precision optics
• Experience with instrumentation involving biological sample processing
• Experience using OpenCV for camera sensing / computer vision applications
• Strong background in performance optimization to ensure deterministic execution of pre-defined software protocols
• Experience developing / interfacing with backend software for instrument data storage and network transmission

title: Staff Mechanical Engineer - Future Opportunity
description:
At Intuitive, we are united behind our mission: we believe that minimally invasive care is life-enhancing care. Through ingenuity and intelligent technology, we expand the potential of physicians to heal without constraints.
As a pioneer and market leader in robotic-assisted surgery, we strive to foster an inclusive and diverse team, committed to making a difference. For more than 25 years, we have worked with hospitals and care teams around the world to help solve some of healthcare's hardest challenges and advance what is possible.
Intuitive has been built by the efforts of great people from diverse backgrounds. We believe great ideas can come from anywhere. We strive to foster an inclusive culture built around diversity of thought and mutual respect. We lead with inclusion and empower our team members to do their best work as their most authentic selves.
Passionate people who want to make a difference drive our culture. Our team members are grounded in integrity, have a strong capacity to learn, the energy to get things done, and bring diverse, real world experiences to help us think in new ways. We actively invest in our team members to support their long-term growth so they can continue to advance our mission and achieve their highest potential.
Join a team committed to taking big leaps forward for a global community of healthcare professionals and their patients. Together, let's advance the world of minimally invasive care.
The Staff Mechanical Design Engineer independently owns technically demanding mechanical and electromechanical subsystems for robotic systems. You will lead subsystem architecture and detailed-design decisions, resolve complex multidisciplinary problems, and contribute to integration decisions beyond your assigned subsystem.
This is a hands-on individual contributor role combining mechanical design ownership with technical guidance and mentorship. The role reports to a Manager of Mechanical Design Engineering in New Product Development.
Essential Job Duties
Own subsystem development from concept through verification and design transfer, including mechanical requirements, specifications, design-risk analyses and verification documentation. Support validation activities with the responsible functions.
Lead subsystem architecture decisions. Compare alternatives and justify tradeoffs.
Design precision mechanisms, joints and actuation assemblies. Select and size components such as motors, bearings, transmissions, brakes and sensors based on operating loads, motion requirements and expected life.
Use first-principles calculations and simulation to establish load paths, component margins, structural stiffness, dynamic behavior and fatigue life. Check assumptions and correlate models with test results.
Create and release CAD models, manufacturing drawings and design documentation. Apply GD&T and tolerance analysis to functional interfaces, assembly requirements and inspection.
Build, test, debug and iterate prototypes. Develop test methods and fixtures, investigate failures, and verify corrective actions.
Work directly with suppliers, supplier engineering, sourcing and manufacturing to resolve technical issues, improve DFM/DFA and cost, and prepare designs for transfer.
Collaborate with systems, electrical, controls, clinical, human factors, manufacturing, supplier engineering/sourcing, quality and regulatory partners to resolve requirements and subsystem interfaces.
Lead technical reviews and guide other engineers’ design and analysis approaches. Plan technical work across functions, set priorities, resolve risks and mentor engineers through problem-solving.
Required Skills and Experience
Experience developing robotic or complex electromechanical products in a regulated industry, with demonstrated independent subsystem ownership from concept through design transfer.
Working knowledge of design controls, risk management, verification and validation.
Deep expertise in first-principles mechanics and precision mechanisms, with demonstrated ability to perform stiffness, dynamics and fatigue analysis.
Proficiency in GD&T, tolerancing, materials, DFM/DFA and manufacturing processes.
Experience designing rotary or linear joints, sizing components, and justifying decisions through analysis; integrating actuation and sensing; and collaborating effectively with controls and electrical engineers.
Hands-on prototyping experience, including assembly, testing, debugging, and rapid iterations.
Proficient with CAD, simulation, and PLM tools such as SolidWorks, ANSYS, and Windchill.
Demonstrated technical leadership through design reviews, cross-functional decision-making, stakeholder influence and engineer mentorship.
Experience with risk management activities including FMEA, risk mitigation, and reliability assessments.
Required Education and Training
Required: Typical minimum Bachelor’s degree plus 14 years of relevant experience, or a Master’s degree plus 10 years, or a PhD plus 6 years.
Preferred: Master’s or PhD degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline.
Working Conditions
On-site four days per week in Sunnyvale, CA.
May involve extended periods of computer-based design and analysis work.
Must be comfortable occasionally working in lab environments, including prototype assembly, mechanical testing, and safe use of standard mechanical tools and fixtures.
Must be able to occasionally lift and handle 25 pounds.
Travel: 10%, including occasional visits to supplier and manufacturing sites.
Preferred Skills and Experience
The following skills and experience are not required but represent attributes of an ideal candidate.
Experience developing Class II or Class III medical devices, particularly surgical robotics or medical device capital equipment.
Direct application of standards and documentation frameworks such as ISO 13485, FDA QMSR (21 CFR Part 820), IEC 60601, ISO 14971, and DHF.
Experience supporting production launch, manufacturing scale-up or post-launch reliability investigations, and applying those lessons to new product designs.

The successful candidate will have the ability to lead a team, and understand and solve complex issues associated with the supplier manufacturing process, quality, and business inter-relationships. This person will develop supplier quality systems and manufacturing processes to sustain suppliers and parts effectively.

Lead a team of supplier engineers in strategic supplier selection, evaluation, development, and improvement with the goal of establishing and maintaining a high-performing, long-term, sustainable production supply chain.

None

Plastics Injection Molding Process Development Knowledge

Silicone/Elastomer Processing Knowledge

Join Multi-Port System Design Engineering, the team that brought the da Vinci 5 system to life and is building what comes next. Learn more at https://careers.intuitive.com/en/career-opportunities/engineering/multiport-engineering/
Primary Function of Position
Systems Analysts (Robotic Algorithms and Control) at Intuitive Surgical perform a central role in the design, development, and support of new products in the daVinci Surgery product line. Systems Analysts are primarily responsible for the tele-robotic motion control algorithms, robotic manipulator control, interaction behaviors, and safety algorithms for new surgical robots and surgical instruments. This responsibility crosses into electrical, mechanical, software, control, user interface, and safety engineering where all the subsystems are integrated together. Systems Analysts strive to provide early design input, quickly prove out new designs, and seek out solutions to subtle and challenging problems in system integration and motion control. Responsibilities continue until the products are shipping to customers with the highest quality and reliability.
Essential Job Duties
Contribute to design of new surgical platforms and instruments through control system analysis and characterization of prototypes.
Design and implement motion algorithms and behaviors.
Apply control theory to the design and verification of mechatronic and tele-robotic systems.
Analyze complex electro-mechanical devices for dynamic safety and clinical risk.
Create safety monitoring algorithms based on sound physics.
Participate in clinical observations and experiments to ensure that performance requirements are relevant and realistic.
Document and pursue intellectual property.
Communicate system performance to the organization as a whole.
Improve group work-flow through tool building and teaching others.
Support and track system performance as it moves from design through manufacturing.
Participate in clinical observations and experiments to ensure performance requirements are relevant, measurable, and realistic.
Required Skills and Experience
Advanced knowledge of classical and modern control theory, with hands-on experience implementing control systems in safety critical products.
Demonstrated experience with robotic manipulation algorithms, including learning-based/ML approaches.
Strong embedded C/C++ and system integration experience (hardware + firmware/software + mechanisms).
Strong engineering intuition for mechatronic systems, paired with attention to detail and the ability to drive solutions to completion.
Ability to excel in a high-energy team environment, with strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently while balancing collaboration on project planning, execution, and communication.
Passion for product quality and continuous improvements.
Required Education and Training
3 years experience and a Master’s degree; or a PhD with 1 years experience; or equivalent experience.

*Please note: Candidates must live within or be willing to relocate to one of the following areas to perform the duties of this role: Nashville, Knoxville, Birmingham, or Huntsville.
Primary Function of Position
The da Vinci® Urology Gynecology Sales Manager (UGSM) plays a critical role in driving specialty-focused adoption and utilization within Urology (URO) and Gynecology (GYN) across their assigned market or markets. The major responsibilities are to build, lead, and develop a high-performing specialty sales team that grows procedure adoption and deepens utilization of the da Vinci Surgical Systems among URO and GYN surgeons within the installed base, while cultivating new surgeon adoption in these specialties. This team must operate with an elevated level of sales acumen and drive, unlocking greater adoption in one of Intuitive's largest procedure opportunities.
A defining feature of this role is close collaboration with overlapping Clinical Sales Managers (CSMs) to align on shared market strategies, account planning, and territory execution. The UGSM will leverage all ISI Ecosystem resources, including Digital, Field Engineering, Genesis, marketing, and MACA, to support these efforts.
Essential Job Duties
Sales Strategy and Business Development
Develop and execute a robust specialty sales strategy for Urology and Gynecology to exceed performance goals and drive utilization of the da Vinci® Surgical Systems while maintaining existing use across URO and GYN service lines and hospitals.
Expand the URO and GYN user base by cultivating a training pipeline of new urology and gynecology surgeons.
Collaborate with overlapping CSMs to develop coordinated market strategies and account plans, ensuring specialty growth objectives align with broader market and territory priorities.
Exhibit proficiency in multiple technology platforms to effectively support dV adoption of Multiport, Single Port, digital solutions, and the specific needs of URO and GYN customers.
Promote advanced instruments and accessories relevant to urologic and gynecologic procedures to enhance surgical performance and promote surgeon autonomy.

Problem Solving & Loss Elimination

Works cross-functionally with the entire plant — CI Manager, Plant Manager, Trios, Functional Managers, Plant/Line 5S Champions, Team Leaders, Operators, and Maintenance Technicians.

Strong facilitation and root-cause analysis skills tied to OEE and loss-elimination outcomes.

Primary schedule is day shift; must be available and willing to work all shifts (including off-shifts and weekends as needed) to deliver training, conduct health checks, and support problem-solving across the full operation.

description:
Job Description:
Job Description
Changing the World, One Kibble at a Time
Champion Petfoods is expanding! We are excited to announce we are looking for a Demand Finance Business Partner, North America to join our rapidly growing company.
Champion Petfoods is an award-winning pet food crafter with a reputation of trust spanning 35+ years. From our humble beginnings, founded in a small town in Alberta, Canada, Champion – with its ORIJEN® and ACANA® brands – is a key player in the global premium pet food industry.
Our purpose,  To Earn Pet Lover Trust Every Day so Pets Thrive for a Lifetime ,  provides the foundation for our highest aspirations as a company. Being a partner to the communities that surround us – and the environment that sustains us – are top priorities.
We would love to hear from you if you are passionate about personal and professional growth and see yourself as a key player contributing to our continued success as an award-winning company.
Here’s the scoop - Summary
The Demand Finance Business Partner, North America is a key strategic and commercial partner responsible for supporting the sales and demand functions in delivering their business and financial objectives. This role bridges commercial ambition with financial execution, serving as a trusted partner to the North American sales. marketing and leadership teams.
Balancing customer/channel dynamics, portfolio mix, pricing strategy, and trade promotions to drive sustainable growth is a central expectation of this role. Operating at the intersection of finance and commercial strategy, this position requires an analytically rigorous and commercially sharp professional who can turn complex datasets into actionable recommendations.
The role is both strategic and tactical, requiring the ability to identify high-level trends and risks while maintaining a hands-on approach to uncover root-cause insights and manage trade budget stewardship.
The Senior Manager, FP&A works out of our Corporate office in or Nashville (TN), Louisville (CO) or New York City (NY) and works a hybrid schedule with 3 days in-person and reports to the Finance Director, NORAM.
Key Responsibilities:
​ Commercial Performance & Revenue Optimization
Channel & Customer Profitability: Lead the review, analysis, and optimization of channel-specific and customer-specific profitability. Develop and maintain transparent performance views to highlight risk areas and unlock growth opportunities.
Route to Market & Portfolio Analysis: Analyze and optimize Route to Market (RTM) structures and portfolio margin profiles in close collaboration with Category Management and sales leadership.
Pricing & Revenue Management: Partner with the Strategic Revenue Management (SRM) team to execute pricing strategies, evaluate promotional elasticity, and ensure commercial alignment with overall financial targets.
Channel Specific Financial Support: Partner with the specific sales channels to model performance, evaluate go-to-market strategies, and drive Net Sales Value (NSV) and Gross Sales Value (GSV) optimization.
Trade Investment & Budget Stewardship
Trade Expenditure Management: Oversee the planning, forecasting, tracking, and controlling of the Trade Expenditure budget to ensure optimal financial discipline.
Promotion Effectiveness & ROI: Establish robust analysis frameworks to evaluate trade promotion effectiveness, measure spending efficiency, and maximize return on investment (ROI).
Accrual & Close Governance: Evaluate and assess outstanding trade expense commitments to inform trade accruals during the periodic close process ensuring compliance with internal governance.
Overhead & A&CP Partnership: Provide financial governance over commercial overhead structures and partner with marketing teams to manage Advertising & Consumer Promotion (A&CP) budgets and drive actionable insights
Integrated Business Planning & S&OP+ Integration
S&OP+ Demand Management Review (DMR): Serve as the core finance representative for Step 2 of the S&OP+ cycle (Demand Management Review). Synthesize operating plans and market assumptions to align sales forecasts with corporate financial commitments.
Strategic Business Planning: Conduct market research, financial modeling, and scenario analysis to assist in the development and execution of the annual and multi-year Business Plans.
Innovation Evaluation: Provide financial assessments, business case modeling, and post-launch performance analysis for local innovation pipelines to ensure margin-accretive growth.
Financial Analysis, Reporting & Performance Tracking
Forecast & Trend Analysis: Provide timely and accurate financial forecasts, month-end variance analyses, and commentary regarding prevailing business trends and market drivers.
Performance Indicators: Define, calculate, and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs), financial benchmarks, and performance scorecards to hold the commercial business accountable.
Executive & Ad Hoc Reporting: Prepare executive-ready reports, business reviews, and ad hoc financial analyses to support key decisions by the leadership team.
Collaboration & Team Leadership
Cross-Functional Partnership: Build trusted relationships across Sales, Marketing, Category Management, and Demand teams, providing both constructive challenge and financial leadership.
Global FP&A Liaison: Collaborate with Regional and Global FP&A teams to integrate local performance reporting into global rhythms and standardize financial frameworks.
Staff Guidance: Provide coaching, training, and professional guidance to junior finance staff or cross-functional team members to elevate financial acumen across the organization.

Preferred: MBA, CPA, CA, or equivalent professional credentials.
Experience Professional Experience: 6+ years of progressive finance experience, with a heavy emphasis on commercial finance, sales finance, trade management, or financial planning.
Industry Context: Experience within a Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG), Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG), or Food & Beverage environment is highly preferred.

The Facilities Technician is responsible for the operation and reliability of all plant systems including high pressure boilers, chillers, cooling towers, air compressors, HVAC systems, Wastewater Treatment (WWT), Ammonia, and facility power supply equipment and processes. The Facilities Technician must possess multi-craft skills (Mechanical and Electrical) and be able to troubleshoot and make repairs to a wide variety of equipment in a safe and efficient manner. This role requires knowledge, competency, professionalism, and safety consciousness to optimize equipment efficiency and longevity while assuring product quality. The Facilities Technician must be able to function with little or no supervision.
This position is responsible for local, state, and federal environmental compliance through internal and external audits and networking with regulators, insurers, and other industry representatives. The Utilities Technician assures adherence to ISO and Mars Wrigley Confectionery Conservation standards. Requirements also include the areas of reliable routine service, timely backlog management and prompt emergency response. The Facilities Technician provides technical knowledge for diagnosing, troubleshooting, repairing and debugging complex utilities issues, computer systems, and/or software. They perform emergency repairs on utilities equipment in a quick, efficient, and safe manner, continuously makes decisions in order of prioritizing tasks to sustain plant operations and production.
Key Responsibilities:
Provide & maintains Steam, Compressed Air, Plant Environmental Conditioning, Fire Protection, Weather protection, and Wastewater Treatment, crucial to plant operation.
Demonstrated expertise in advanced troubleshooting and resolution of system-wide or area-wide, chronic problems in processes and products.
Ensures that the jobs listed in the Daily Shift Checks manual are performed efficiently and in a timely manner. This consists of but is not limited to: Shift checks and logging of equipment operation, chemical testing of boiler and loop systems, assuring safe and efficient operation as well as maintenance of the Boilers and their sub equipment, Chillers and sub equipment, Air compressors and sub equipment, Environmental Air Handler units and sub equipment as well as assist at the WWT if needed.
Ensure adherence to the various operating permits and required inspections mandated by Federal, State, and Local authorities. These include Air, Wastewater, Pressure Vessels, Refrigeration, Storm water and Spill Prevention Control and Countermeasure Plan, by actively following ISO 9000/14001 Standards.
Ensure optimum efficiency of all plant utilities, and wastewater equipment, through preventive/predictive methods. We highly value the dedication, safety-first mindset, and structured teamwork developed in the military and look forward to helping you build a successful civilian career.
Job Summary
The Material Handler is responsible for the end-to-end logistics flow within our plant. This dual-focus role handles all incoming packaging and raw ingredients, manages safe product movement inside the site, loads outbound trailers for shipment, completes all logistics paperwork, and maintains perfect inventory control. This associate works closely with production, purchasing, receiving, shipping, and quality teams to ensure seamless plant operations in a clean, temperature-controlled environment.
Key Responsibilities
Receiving & Inbound Logistics
Receive and verify all incoming raw materials, ingredients, packaging, and components against purchase orders and shipping manifests.
Use a forklift to safely unload inbound trucks and transfer materials to their correct designated storage locations.
Conduct strict quality and food safety checks on incoming materials, including collecting product samples and verifying supplier paperwork.
Collaborate with external logistics departments and freight carriers to ensure correct and safe delivery of production materials.
Material Handling & Warehouse Operations
Safely and accurately operate material handling equipment (including forklifts) to transport inventory, raw materials, WIP (work-in-process), and finished goods throughout the facility.
Support production schedules by ensuring that the correct materials are issued and staged in production areas when needed.
Stage, build, and load outbound trailers for shipment, ensuring proper cargo weight distribution and trailer utilization.
Ensure proper labeling, sorting, FIFO (First-In, First-Out) rotation, and general organization of all materials in storage areas.
Inventory, Systems, & Documentation
Scan and track material movements using warehouse management systems to ensure perfect real-time inventory accountability.
Perform daily cycle counts, participate in precision monthly inventories, and assist with formal physical audits.
Investigate inventory discrepancies promptly and report findings to management.
Generate, review, and complete accurate shipping/receiving paperwork, logging all transactions accurately into the plant database.
Safety, Quality, & Food Safety Culture
Participate and adhere to all food safety requirements, Quality Management Processes (QMPs), and site safety programs, championing a safety-first culture.
Maintain a clean, organized, and sanitary warehouse environment in accordance with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs).
Promptly report any safety, food safety, or quality concerns to leadership.
Position Requirements
Minimum Qualifications:
Education: High school diploma, GED, or equivalent civilian/military education.
Experience: Proven experience in warehouse logistics, receiving, shipping, or material handling roles.
Equipment: Demonstrated experience operating a forklift safely in an industrial or warehouse environment.
Physical Ability: Must be in good physical condition with the ability to stand and walk for extended periods, bend, reach, climb, and safely lift up to 40 pounds manually.
Technical Literacy: Working knowledge of basic computer programs for entering data, record keeping, and maintaining inventory logs.
Core Skills: Basic math skills, a keen eye for detail, strong organizational skills, and excellent written and verbal communication abilities.
Teamwork: Demonstrated ability to work in a high-performing team environment with a willingness to learn and be coached.
Military & Veteran Technical Equivalency Guide
At Mars, we recognize that your military service has prepared you to excel in logistical operations. Your training in high-stakes material movement, precision inventory tracking, and supply chain management maps directly to this role. If you served in any of the following specialties, we highly encourage you to apply:
U.S. Army: Automated Logistical Specialist (92A), Unit Supply Specialist (92Y), Cargo Specialist (88H), Motor Transport Operator (88M), Ammunition Specialist (89B). Your experience with warehouse databases, material handling equipment (MHE), and precise property book audits is an excellent fit.
U.S. Navy: Logistics Specialist (LS), Storekeeper, Aviation Storekeeper (AK). Your experience managing inventory, shipboard supply warehouses, and processing shipping manifests maps directly to our material tracking systems.
U.S. Air Force: Materiel Management (2S0X1), Traffic Management (2T0X1), Ground Transportation (2T1X1). Your training in cargo loading, receiving inspections, strict compliance with safety procedures, and inventory precision is an exact match.
U.S. Marine Corps: Warehouse Clerk (3051), Supply Administration & Operations (3043), Logistics/Embarkation Specialist (0431), Motor Vehicle Operator (3531). Your focus on cargo staging, load planning, and material handling equipment matches our shipping and receiving operations.
U.S. Coast Guard: Storekeeper (SK), Marine Science Technician.
What We Offer (Total Rewards & Benefits)
At Mars, being an associate is more than a job—it's an opportunity to build a long-term career. We provide a competitive, industry-leading package starting on your very first day:
Compensation: Competitive base pay based on experience, shift differentials, and significant overtime (OT) potential.
Annual Bonus: Eligibility for our annual performance-based company bonus and annual merit increases.
Health & Wellness: Comprehensive Medical, Vision, and Dental insurance starting on Day One.
Retirement Planning: An exceptional 401(k) program with up to 6% company match.
Work-Life Balance: Generous paid vacation time, paid holidays, and predictable rotating 2-2-3 day shifts.
Family Support: Paid Parental Leave, plus Short-Term and Long-Term Disability.
Career Growth: Access to top-tier learning and development through Mars University.
Onsite Perks: Access to our onsite gym.
About Mars, Incorporated
Mars is a family-owned business with over a century of history making diverse products and offering services for people and the pets people love. We produce some of the world’s best-loved brands: M&M’s®, SNICKERS®, TWIX®, MILKY WAY®, DOVE®, PEDIGREE®, ROYAL CANIN®, WHISKAS®, EXTRA®, ORBIT®, 5™, SKITTLES®, BEN’S ORIGINAL®, and COCOAVIA®.
Alongside our consumer brands, we proudly take care of half of the world’s pets through our nutrition, health, and services businesses such as Banfield Pet Hospitals™, BluePearl®, Linnaeus, AniCura, VCA™, and Pet Partners™.
The Mars Five Principles – Quality, Responsibility, Mutuality, Efficiency, and Freedom – inspire our 130,000 Associates to take action every day toward creating the world we want tomorrow.

Responsibilities
Datacenter Operations
Complies with Data Center business unit policies, procedures, and deadlines with guidance from experienced technicians and/or direct-line management. Escalates issues related to compliance or operational assurance activities to direct-line management.
Reviews Process Change Notifications (PCNs) and develops an understanding of the impact to work execution and awareness to changes within their area of work and/or the work of others. Asks questions when they do not have required information and may provide feedback on changes to processes to experienced technicians and/or direct-line management.
Completes assigned tickets efficiently and in alignment with relevant Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) per task type with guidance from experienced technicians. Seeks guidance from more experienced technicians on challenging or complex tickets.
Receives guidance and supervision to develop an understanding of standard processes and procedures for preparing, installing, performing diagnostics, troubleshooting, replacing, and/or decommissioning IT datacenter technology(ies) and equipment. Develops and acquires a fundamental understanding of the functions of, and interactions between cabling infrastructure, network, server, and storage equipment.
Datacenter Work Environment Completes required security and data management training while complying with security and data management procedures/policies with guidance from other technicians. May escort third party vendors or IT support on-premises at data centers or network sites. Appropriately takes action and reports physical security access concerns and/or incidents to direct-line management or established reporting methods.
Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
Contributes to a positive and effective team environment by sharing information with other shifts or technician teams, contributing in regular team meetings, asking questions, and partnering with other shifts of technician teams to complete smooth transition and effective handover of ticketed work. Encourages providing and responding to feedback received on ways to work more effectively or enhance efficiency within their team and adopts best practices shared within-and-across shifts or technician teams.
Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.

Completes required Environmental & Health Safety (EHS) training, complies with safety procedures (e.g., equipment use, lifting, electrical hazards, ladder/rolling stair use), completes required Task Hazard Analysis (THAs), and uses appropriate equipment and Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for assigned tasks. Adheres to and promotes a culture of safety, taking proactive action to alert others of safety concerns, near-misses, and/or incidents. Participates in regular cadence proactive safety observation reporting processes and systems.
Traveling up to 25% typically domestically to and from multiple locations during the workday, and occasionally domestically to other sites for overnight stays. May work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.

Develops an understanding of cross-functional Data Center processes to support partnerships with internal and external stakeholders.
Completes required training aligned to job focus areas and workloads (i.e., Break fix, Deployment, Simple Change, Decommission, IT Critical Environment) in a timely manner per direct-line management assignment(s). Observes more experienced technicians to gain hands-on experience and relevant on-the-job training (OJT). May complete additional or supplemental training to obtain or maintain relevant industry or technical certifications.
Escalates and/or seeks guidance from experienced technicians or direct-line management regarding client interactions.
Service Delivery Develops an understanding of effective execution order strategy(ies) for assigned tasks with assistance from experienced technicians or direct-line management. Prepares, stages, sets up, and performs basic startups and shutdowns for hardware (e.g., racks, hard drives, switches) according to specific written instructions provided via checklists, guides, standard processes, emails, guidance from other technicians, and/or direction from management. May perform tasks in tandem with other technicians to comply with procedures and safety requirements.

Follows procedures to immediately communicate, report, and escalate data center technical or safety related incidents to direct-line management. May participate in bridge calls to provide details on incident status and executes on-site follow-up actions as directed if necessary.
Learns about post-execution verification of grounding, staging, labeling, and cabling to align with all safety protocols, deployment standards, and planned Network Design Templates (NDTs). Learns about errors in deployment standards or Network Design Templates (NDTs) and escalates to relevant technicians or specialists to coordinate corrections as needed.
Performs basic diagnostics and troubleshooting with guidance from experienced technicians and/or via standard procedures to identify the cause(s) of technical issues and replace faulty components in network, storage, or server equipment with zero-to-minimal customer and/or business disruption. Develops awareness of conditions, circumstances, and scenarios which may reflect significant customer or business impact within the Data Center environment.
Other
Embody our culture and values
Qualifications
Required Qualifications: High school diploma, GED, or equivalent and basic knowledge of computer hardware and components  OR equivalent experience.
Other Requirements: Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings: Microsoft Cloud Background Check:  This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

Own end-to-end three-dimensional (3D) computer-aided design (CAD) for cryogenic subassemblies and top-level mechanical integrations, including cold fingers, millikelvin (mK) and 4 kelvin (4 K) stages, radiation shields, vacuum interfaces, and cable or harness routing fixtures; create fully detailed two-dimensional (2D) drawings with geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) and tolerance stackups.

Create SOPs by making detailed work instructions for installing parts, recording key data during installation and making sure that engineering intent is effectively communicated to engineers and technicians in the field.
Drive design for manufacturing/design for excellence (DFM/DFX) with suppliers by generating clear build packages, supporting fabrication through first-article approval, dispositioning nonconformances with data-driven tolerance and fit assessments, and capturing as-built changes in drawings and bills of materials (BOMs).

Built on Microsoft’s core platforms and delivered through and with a global ecosystem of partners and customers, this platform accelerates AI for the physical world and helps robotics solutions move from experimentation to reliable, scaled deployment.
We are hiring a Member of Technical Staff to contribute to the design, development, and testing of core infrastructure components of the Microsoft Robotics platform, including the Software Development Kits (SDKs), cloud services, edge runtimes, developer tooling, and agent orchestration layers that enable people, AI agents, and robots to operate together across end-to-end mission workflows. Implement and test features within core platform components with guidance, including robotics SDKs, cloud-hosted Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), edge runtimes, and agent orchestration frameworks that enable developers and partners to compose interoperable autonomy capabilities (perception, planning, control, multi-agent coordination) into deployable mission workflows.

Help test and investigate performance against the latency requirements of real-time robotic control loops.
Help improve the developer experience for the Microsoft Robotics platform by contributing Command Line Interface (CLI) features, SDK functionality, documentation, sample code, and inner-loop workflow improvements, following team patterns and incorporating feedback from internal developers and external partners.
Use AI-assisted development tools, such as GitHub Copilot, and agentic coding workflows to improve engineering productivity and software quality. Contribute to agent-based engineering solutions that automate repetitive tasks, accelerate investigation and root cause analysis, and strengthen testing, validation, and operational reliability, applying team standards for code review and verification of AI-generated changes.
Collaborate with autonomy, simulation, and evaluation teams to understand requirements and implement and test assigned features in platform primitives (compute orchestration, data routing, model serving, experiment tracking), helping support the performance, reliability, and reproducibility needs of Machine Learning (ML) training, sim-to-real transfer, and online evaluation workloads.

title: Principal Applied Scientist
location: United States, Washington, Redmond; United States, California, Mountain View
description:
Overview
The Online Forensics team sits within the Microsoft AI Experiences organization, where we protect the monetization network that funds the products people use every day. Because attackers adapt quickly, effective defense requires discovering how systems can be abused, not just investigating known incidents. We combine hands-on adversarial research, controlled experimentation, and large-scale data analysis to establish authoritative ground truth and expose weaknesses before they are exploited at scale.
As a Principal Applied Scientist, you will discover how web-based monetization systems can be manipulated and build the experimental and investigation systems needed to study that abuse at scale. Your research will cover both exploitable weaknesses and abuse of intended functionality, including automation, identity and attribution manipulation, and multi-step economic exploitation. You will personally write code, construct safe adversarial experiments, and combine experimental evidence with large-scale telemetry to establish mechanism, prevalence, and impact.
The scientific challenge is to distinguish adversarial manipulation from legitimate behavior under incomplete and potentially manipulated telemetry. You will develop methods to test competing explanations, determine whether experimental findings generalize to real-world traffic, and evaluate candidate signals without unacceptable false positives. You will turn validated approaches into reliable, reusable systems and evaluation methods that partner defense teams can adopt.
You will own a focused portfolio of high-impact research problems, from hypothesis through implementation, validation, and adoption. At the principal level, you will set scientific and technical direction while remaining directly involved in coding, experimentation, debugging, and delivery. You will own the research capabilities you build; partner defense teams own production enforcement and remediation.
Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Discover and validate abuse mechanisms. Form original, testable hypotheses about adversarial manipulation of web and advertising systems and emerging LLM-native monetization flows. Investigate system behavior, service interactions, and economic incentives to explain how the abuse works.
Personally implement adversarial experiments. Build automated clients, instrumented browser workflows, simulations, and replay harnesses under safe, authorized conditions with clear scope and safeguards. Use appropriate controls and competing hypotheses to distinguish demonstrated mechanisms from unvalidated assumptions.
Develop rigorous evaluation methods. Assess whether experiments represent real-world conditions, establish the provenance and quality of labels, and measure generalization, coverage, false-positive risk, and robustness to adaptation.
Build durable research and investigation systems. Design, implement, test, deploy, and maintain the services, instrumentation, telemetry pipelines, and reusable libraries needed for the research portfolio. Turn successful approaches into reliable capabilities that other researchers and partner teams can use independently.
Connect experiments to real-world evidence. Apply behavioral, graph-based, temporal, and cross-surface analysis to large-scale telemetry. Identify adversary infrastructure and evasion patterns, determine prevalence, and quantify economic exposure while stating uncertainty and limitations.
Establish authoritative ground truth. Correlate evidence across accounts, traffic, transactions, providers, devices, and infrastructure. Reconstruct attack chains and produce reproducible datasets and technical assessments that clearly state mechanism, provenance, confidence, scale, and impact.
Translate findings into stronger defenses. Produce candidate signals, labeled evaluation datasets, monitored indicators, and reproducible regression scenarios. Partner with teams that own production defenses to evaluate improvements and verify that corrective actions address the demonstrated abuse.

We are building the next generation of that network. That means rethinking how the optical, packet and control layers work together, moving more of the network onto open hardware and software we control, and bringing new optical and fiber technologies into production as they mature. It also means changing how the physical network itself is built and maintained, using automation and robotics to make that work faster, safer and more consistent.
As a Principal Cloud Network Engineer, you will help decide what this network becomes and then take it into production. You will own significant parts of the next generation architecture, drive the disaggregation of the hardware the network runs on, and help lead how automation and robotics change the way physical infrastructure is built and operated. This is a role for someone who wants to work across the boundaries between light, packets, software and the physical world, on a network that can never be taken offline.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Next Generation Network Design: Own significant parts of the multi-year architecture for Azure's global network across the optical, packet and control layers. Design so that capacity, topology and protection can each evolve independently, and so that no single change or failure can reach the entire backbone.
Hardware Disaggregation: Help move the network from vendor-integrated systems to open, interchangeable building blocks: merchant silicon, open network operating systems such as SONiC, open optical line systems, and pluggable and co-packaged optics. Define requirements, evaluate platforms, and work with silicon vendors, ODMs and optical suppliers to shape their roadmaps years ahead of availability.
Programmable Optical Layer: Drive how optical circuit switching, optical protection switching, coherent transport and hollow core fiber become active parts of the network design. Define the interfaces, telemetry and control models that let software see, reason about and act on the physical layer.
Physical Automation and Robotics: Find where automation and robotics can make the physical network faster, safer and more consistent to build and repair: inspection, installation quality, fiber and connector handling, hardware qualification, and repetitive lab and technician work. Run focused pilots with clear quality, safety and cost goals, and turn the ones that work into how we build.
Simulation and Safe Change: Prove designs before anything physical moves. Use and extend network simulation, digital twins and lab automation so that architectures, capacity plans and changes are validated before they reach production. Help define which physical actions can be automated, which require human approval, and which should always stay human.
AI-Driven Engineering: Apply AI and agents to our own engineering, across design, qualification, deployment and operations, so that engineers spend their time on architecture rather than on process.
Concept to Production: Take ideas from paper to lab to pilot to fleet. Write the design, build or direct the prototype, define the qualification, and stay with it through deployment at global scale.
Technical Leadership and Influence: Lead across Azure engineering, hardware, supply chain, datacenter operations, Microsoft Research and external partners without relying on reporting lines. Mentor engineers, raise the technical bar, and communicate trade-offs clearly to engineers, vendors and senior leaders.
Qualifications

Doctorate Degree in Electrical Engineering, Optical Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field AND 3+ years technical experience in network design, development, and automation OR Master's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Optical Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field AND 4+ years technical experience in network design, development, and automation

description:

Compliance Management - The ability to supervise and observe the organization's conformity to various standards, procedures, rules, and regulations.
Project Quality Assurance - Knowledge of and the ability to apply systematic and continuing processes of making sure that the project is meeting specified requirements.
Quality Assurance - Knowledge of and the ability to follow systematic and continuing processes of checking to see whether a product, service, or process is meeting specified requirements. This includes knowledge of quality measurements and defined standards.
Regulatory Compliance - Knowledge of the rules, regulations, sanctions and other statutory requirements, guidelines and instructions relating to local and/or international governing bodies and organizations, both internally and externally.
Risk Analysis - Knowledge of Risk Management and Analysis, the process of measuring, or assessing risk and then developing strategies to manage the risk. Construction Planning and Logistics
Construction - Knowledge of materials, methods, and the tools involved in the construction, repair, and engineering of buildings, houses, or other structures such as highways, roads, and bridges.
Construction Consulting - The ability to provide management, risk-based advisory, dispute resolution and strategic communications services across all construction and engineering.
Construction Management - Knowledge of specialized, project management techniques to oversee the planning, design, and construction of a project, from its beginning to its end.
Construction Planning - The ability to plan how the team will manage and execute a construction project.
Construction Processes - Knowledge of the design process (creating the description of a new facility, usually represented by detailed plans and specifications) and the construction planning process (identifying activities and resources required to make the design a physical reality).
Scope Management - The ability to manage scope over the course of a project, including determining which changes are essential, estimating their impact on the project, ensuring that changes do not expand scope beyond acceptable levels, and keeping a change record to track progress.

Budgeting - Knowledge of and the ability to develop and utilize budgeting guidelines, practices, and techniques, including forecasting. Project Cost - Knowledge of the process of identifying project resources, estimating costs, developing the budget, and managing the finances for a project.
Managing Vendor and Stakeholder Relationships
Conflict Resolution
The ability to manage conflict, disharmony, and strife among people and situations, while recognizing and addressing sensitivities.
Incident Handling - The ability to lead and direct others in the process of resolving escalated problems through communication.
Influence Others - The ability to garner support for initiatives by gaining the respect of others and inspiring trust and confidence.
Negotiation - The ability to achieve mutually satisfying agreements in negotiations with others by listening to their objectives, acting as the company's representative to effectively communicate the company's objective, and seeking common ground and collaborative solutions.
Team Facilitation - The ability to lead and orchestrate cross-functional teams to complete objectives. This includes the skills of communicating and collaborating with others, leveraging resources and tools, and coordinating processes.

Change Management - The ability to define and implement procedures and/or technologies to deal with changes in the environment. This may include adapting to change, controlling change, and/or affecting change.
Decision Making - The ability to make decisions in a fast-paced, rapidly changing environment. This includes the ability to define, diagnose, and determine an appropriate resolution, recommendation, or decision while considering alternatives and factors (e.g., resources, costs, tradeoffs).

title: Principal Data Engineering Architect
description:
Overview
Effective marketing starts with understanding customers: how they engage, what they need, and which experiences create value.  Microsoft's Marketing Data Engineering Team turns signals across web, campaigns, content, seller and partner interactions, and sales outcomes into trusted data products. We help marketers improve multi-channel customer engagement and learn faster through evidence, with AI-native self-service that makes trusted data easier to find and use.
As a Principal Data Engineering Architect , you will lead the architecture and hands-on development of petabyte-scale systems processing billions of events per day that power the business. You will help shape team strategy across data architecture, modeling, solution design and data products, and provide technical direction for major capabilities. This individual contributor role combines autonomy with influence across partner engineering teams, enabling domain teams through shared standards.
Business acumen is central to the role. You will work closely with marketers, marketing technologists, analysts and data scientists to understand their challenges and the why behind requests. Connect customer and business needs to reusable capabilities that solve more than a single requirement, while choosing the simplest approach that delivers value without overbuilding.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. We bring a growth mindset to our work, collaborate across boundaries, and build on the values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create an inclusive culture where everyone can thrive.
Join us to unleash your potential and play a pivotal role as a data innovator with world-changing impact - your journey starts here!
Responsibilities
Business Understanding & Impact
This role enables Microsoft's Marketing organization to transform raw data into trusted, scalable, AI-ready data products that fuel campaign performance measurement, customer intelligence, audience engagement, revenue growth, and executive decision-making through the Microsoft Fabric ecosystem.
The Principal Data Engineering Architect is responsible for the following:
Partner with PMs and business users to define problems, connect requests to customer journeys and business outcomes, and prioritize reusable capabilities. Use feedback, adoption, reuse and quality measures to guide product decisions and team data strategy.
Lead solution design and production implementation of major data capabilities. Build hands-on prototypes, contribute production code, review code, models and designs, and remain accountable for operational reliability and measurable product outcomes.
Develop logical, physical and semantic models for foundational marketing domains. Productize engagement signals with clear business definitions, metric logic, contracts and ownership so analysts, applications and AI consumers can use data without guessing its meaning.
Design distributed processing and storage using streaming, batch or combined patterns. Apply immutable event data and flexible schema evolution to protect downstream products. Make explicit tradeoffs among latency, accuracy, reliability, cost and maintainability.
Influence engineering and user-facing tools for governed self-service ingestion, publishing and extension of platform data. Improve discovery, access and user experience through interoperable templates, interfaces and semantic abstractions that preserve domain ownership.
Embed security, privacy and quality by design, including metadata, lineage, classification, policy-aware access and retention. Establish monitoring and engineering practices that make federated products trustworthy, supportable and cost-conscious throughout their lifecycle.
Advance AI automation and governed code generation for transformations, tests, documentation and self-service data extension. Use bounded assistance for operational detection and recommendations, with rigorous validation, approved remediation and human judgment for consequential changes. Measure delivery and operational improvements.
Bring a startup mindset to a large, complex data environment: listen, simplify, iterate quickly and make sound decisions. Mentor and coach engineers, strengthen reviews and standards, and align partner teams through technical credibility and collaboration.
Other
Embody our  culture  and  values.

title: Senior Mechanical Designer - Cryomechanical Systems
description:
Overview
The Cryomechanical team enables Microsoft Quantum’s hardware roadmap by designing, integrating, and sustaining cryogenic mechanical systems, packaging solutions, and laboratory infrastructure that support reliable experimentation, scalable system integration, and disciplined transition from research concepts to producible hardware.
At Microsoft Quantum, we aim to empower science and scientists to solve the world’s biggest problems by realizing advanced computing platforms at the intersection of high-performance computing, artificial intelligence, and quantum information technology. Microsoft Quantum will change the world of computing and help solve some of humankind’s currently unsolvable problems. For more information about our team, visit https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/quantum .
As a Senior Mechanical Designer – Cryomechanical Systems You will own products from cradle to grave, working hands on to oversee initial builds, incorporating customer feedback to make improvements and driving continuous improvements to equipment as the state-of-the-art advances. You help shape requirements, create complete three-dimensional (3D) models from scratch, produce two-dimensional (2D) drawings, document Bill of Materials (BOM), create standard operating procedures (SOPs) and work hands on in installations to guide products through their entire lifecycle.
Microsoft’s culture is grounded in a growth mindset, customer obsession, diversity and inclusion, one Microsoft collaboration, and making a difference through technology. In this role, you will be expected to model these values by learning continuously, partnering across disciplines, communicating clearly, and creating an inclusive environment where rigorous engineering and shared accountability help the team deliver meaningful impact.
Responsibilities
Own end-to-end three-dimensional (3D) computer-aided design (CAD) for cryogenic subassemblies and top-level mechanical integrations, including cold fingers, millikelvin (mK) and 4 kelvin (4 K) stages, radiation shields, vacuum interfaces, and cable or harness routing fixtures; create fully detailed two-dimensional (2D) drawings with geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) and tolerance stackups.
Build and steward the top assembly and bill of materials (BOM) by managing part numbering, configurations, engineering change order (ECO) and engineering change request (ECR) workflows, and product data management/product lifecycle management (PDM/PLM) toolchains such as SolidWorks, Windchill, and OnePDM.
Lead Cryomechanical Engineering (CryoME) design reviews using standard review packages that include three-dimensional (3D) computer-aided design (CAD), two-dimensional (2D) drawings, critical-to-function specifications, materials, coatings, finishes, incoming quality control (IQC), cryogenic screening plans, manufacturing and assembly flows, risks, and schedules.
Translate system requirements into mechanical specifications for thermal anchoring, heat-load budgets, coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch management, vacuum sealing, vibration isolation, radio frequency (RF) and direct current (DC) cable management, and integration across temperature stages.
