title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
Overview
The Agent 365 Foundation team builds and operates the platform layer that keeps agent workloads reliable, secure, and fast at Microsoft scale. Our charter within this group is traffic ingress: every request that reaches our clusters passes through the gateway and edge systems we own. We are the front door, which means we are also the first line of defense and the first place a problem shows up.
A significant part of our current focus is ingress for Dynamics 365 and Power Platform traffic. That work spans routing and gateway policy, connection and protocol handling, tenant isolation, throttling and abuse mitigation, failover behavior across regions, and the observability needed to reason about all of it while it is happening. The scale is large, the traffic patterns are diverse, and the correctness bar is high.
About the Role
We are hiring a Senior Software Engineer to design, build, and operate the gateway and ingress path end to end. This is a hands-on engineering role. You will spend your time in code, in design reviews, and in production — writing services in C# and Go, tuning TLS and HTTP/2 behavior, shaping how gRPC traffic flows through the stack, working with Azure Front Door and our own edge components, and hardening the system against volumetric and application-layer attacks.
You will own outcomes rather than tickets. That means choosing where resiliency belongs in the request path, deciding what a safe failure mode looks like for a given class of traffic, and defending those decisions with data. You will also be part of the on-call rotation for the systems you build, because the fastest way to build a resilient front door is to feel it when it bends.
Who Thrives in This Role
The engineer who does well here is genuinely hands-on. You are comfortable being the person who reads the proxy source, reproduces the failure locally, and lands the fix — seniority here means more time close to the system, not less. You think critically about problems before reaching for a solution, ask what the data actually shows, and are willing to challenge a design, including your own, when the evidence points elsewhere.
You also do not shy away from hard problems. Ambiguous incidents, legacy traffic paths, unfamiliar protocol behavior, and difficult cross-team conversations are part of the work, and you move toward them rather than around them. You are direct, collaborative, and comfortable operating with a high degree of ownership.
Why This Role Matters
Ingress is where reliability and security are decided for everything behind it. The work you do here is visible in the availability numbers of some of Microsoft's largest business platforms, and it is felt immediately by the customers who depend on them. If you want a role where deep networking expertise, sound judgment, and engineering craft compound into real impact, this is it.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Design, implement, and operate L4 and L7 ingress components — gateways, proxies, load balancing and routing policy — that carry Dynamics 365 and Power Platform traffic into our clusters.
Own the protocol layer: TLS termination and certificate lifecycle, HTTP/2 connection management, gRPC routing and streaming behavior, and the performance characteristics of each.
Build resiliency into the request path through health-based routing, retries and hedging, circuit breaking, load shedding, rate limiting, and regional failover, and prove the behavior through fault injection and load testing.
Strengthen the security posture of the edge, including DDoS detection and mitigation, WAF and abuse-mitigation policy, tenant isolation, and defense against application-layer attack patterns.
Integrate and tune Azure Front Door and related edge services alongside our first-party gateway components, and make deliberate decisions about which layer solves which problem.
Instrument the ingress path so that latency, error, and saturation questions can be answered in minutes, and drive incident response, root-cause analysis, and the follow-through that keeps the same failure from repeating.
Partner with service teams across Dynamics 365, Power Platform, and Agent 365 on onboarding, capacity, and traffic-shaping decisions, and raise the engineering bar through design and code review.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 4+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python OR equivalent experience.
Other Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.
Preferred Qualifications:
Master's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 6+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python OR Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 8+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python
OR equivalent experience.
Proven knowledge of L4 and L7 networking: TCP connection behavior, load balancing, proxying, routing, DNS, and the tradeoffs between transport-level and application-level handling.
Practical depth in TLS, HTTP/2, and gRPC, including certificate management, handshake and connection tuning, multiplexing behavior, and diagnosing protocol-level failures from packet captures and traces.
Production experience with C# or Go, and the willingness to work fluently in both.

description:

At Microsoft Quantum, we aim to empower science and scientists to solve the world’s biggest problems by realizing advanced computing platforms at the intersection of high-performance computing, artificial intelligence, and quantum information technology. The Cryomechanical team enables Microsoft Quantum’s hardware roadmap by designing, integrating, and sustaining cryogenic mechanical systems, packaging solutions, and laboratory infrastructure that support reliable experimentation, scalable system integration, and disciplined transition from research concepts to producible hardware.
As a Simulation Engineer – Mechanical & Thermal Systems , you will lead mechanical, structural, thermal, and coupled multiphysics analysis for cryogenic hardware and laboratory systems using COMSOL Multiphysics and ANSYS. You will translate system requirements and design concepts into verified computational models, quantify margins and sensitivities, correlate predictions with test data, and deliver clear engineering recommendations that guide architecture, detailed design, manufacturing, integration, and root-cause investigations throughout the product lifecycle.
Microsoft’s culture is grounded in a growth mindset, customer obsession, diversity and inclusion, one Microsoft collaboration, and making a difference through technology. In this role, you will be expected to model these values by learning continuously, partnering across disciplines, communicating clearly, and creating an inclusive environment where rigorous engineering and shared accountability help the team deliver meaningful impact.
Responsibilities
Own end-to-end mechanical and thermal analysis for cryogenic subassemblies and top-level integrations, including millikelvin (mK), 4 kelvin (4 K), and ambient-temperature structures, radiation shields, vacuum interfaces, thermal straps, supports, and cable or harness routing hardware.
Develop and maintain high-fidelity finite element and multiphysics models in COMSOL Multiphysics and ANSYS Mechanical, including defensible geometry idealization, material models, contacts, interfaces, meshing strategies, loads, boundary conditions, solver controls, and post-processing methods.

Drive design decisions through clear technical communication by presenting assumptions, methods, limitations, margins, risks, and recommendations at design reviews; partner with mechanical designers, thermal engineers, physicists, electrical engineers, manufacturing teams, and suppliers to close issues and improve designs.

title: Sr. Manufacturing Engineer
location: United States, Washington, Redmond; United States, California, Mountain View
description:
Overview
Microsoft Silicon, Cloud Hardware, and Infrastructure Engineering (SCHIE) is the team behind Microsoft's expanding Cloud Infrastructure and responsible for powering Microsoft's Intelligent Cloud mission. SCHIE delivers the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online businesses, including Microsoft Azure, Office 365, Teams, OneDrive, Xbox Live, Bing, and MSN. Our focus is on smart growth, high efficiency, and delivering trusted experiences to customers and partners worldwide.
As Microsoft's cloud business continues to grow, deploying new hardware infrastructure on time, at high volume, with high quality and competitive cost is increasingly important. The Hardware, Infrastructure Management, and Fundamentals Engineering team defines and delivers operational measures of success for cloud hardware manufacturing, improving planning, quality, delivery, scale, and sustainability.
We are looking for a Senior Hardware Manufacturing Engineer who combines deep manufacturing engineering fundamentals with strategic thinking and disciplined program execution.
The Manufacturing Engineering Group collaborates with Microsoft's suppliers, design engineering teams, quality and reliability teams, business managers, sourcing, and supply chain organizations to ensure new cloud hardware is available to customers on time and at high levels of quality. A critical part of this work is ensuring Microsoft-designed hardware can be built at supplier factories safely, efficiently, repeatedly, and at scale.
In this role, you will lead manufacturing strategy and execution from early design engagement through NPI, qualification, production ramp, and sustaining operations for complex custom-silicon and cloud-hardware platforms, including GPU and AI systems. Particular emphasis will include manufacturing engineering for GPU and AI systems using high-speed optical networking, where optical modules, high-speed cable and fiber assemblies, liquid-cooled trays, rack-level fiber infrastructure, and cross-supplier interoperability create new manufacturing, qualification, reliability, and production-ramp challenges. You will understand product and process details, identify systemic manufacturing risks, translate high-level objectives into executable plans, and deliver results by influencing cross-functional v-teams and external manufacturing partners. You will solve ambiguous technical and operational problems, align diverse stakeholders, establish clear manufacturing plans and metrics, and drive risks to closure across geographically distributed teams.
#azurehwjobs #HIFE
Responsibilities
Manufacturing Technical Leadership : Serve as the senior manufacturing engineering lead for assigned cloud-hardware, GPU, optical-networking, and custom-silicon programs. Own the manufacturing technical strategy from early architecture through sustaining production, ensuring products can be built, tested, repaired, scaled, and supported reliably across global factories.
Design for Manufacturing and Product Industrialization : Lead DFM, DFA, testability, serviceability, packaging, automation, tolerance, and sustainability reviews with design, NPI, quality, reliability, supplier, and factory teams. Identify product and process constraints early, quantify risk, and influence architecture and design decisions to improve manufacturability, yield, cost, reliability, and time to market.
Manufacturing Architecture and Technical Ownership : Serve as the manufacturing technical authority for assigned products and systems. Translate product architecture into production processes, equipment and tooling strategies, assembly sequences, inspection and test methods, process controls, repair boundaries, supplier requirements, and factory qualification plans. Maintain accountability for the technical integrity of the manufacturing solution from early architecture through sustaining production.
GPU and Optical Networking Manufacturing : Lead manufacturing architecture, DFM, process development, and production-readiness activities for GPU and AI systems using optical and high-speed interconnect technologies. Drive manufacturability across optical engines and modules, high-speed electrical flyover cables, multifiber connectors, fiber trunks and shuffle assemblies, accelerator trays, switch trays, rack-level fiber management, liquid cooling, and related infrastructure.
Optical Process Qualification and Factory Test: Develop and qualify contamination-controlled handling, cleaning, inspection, installation, routing, configuration-verification, and test processes for optical and high-speed interconnect assemblies. Establish factory coverage for connector integrity, cable and fiber mapping, optical-path continuity, link bring-up, telemetry, firmware interoperability, power sequencing, cooling integrity, serviceability, and system-level fault isolation.
Optical Supplier and Ramp Readiness : Drive qualification and production readiness across optical-module, laser, connector, cable, fiber-management, rack, cooling, PCB, and contract-manufacturing partners. Own supplier DFM closure, process capability, yield improvement, capacity validation, interoperability, second-source readiness, and contingency planning for maturing optical technologies.
NPI Manufacturing Execution and Technical Leadership : Convert product architecture and roadmaps into integrated manufacturing plans covering prototype builds, EV/ DV/ PV, qualification, and volume ramp. Establish technically grounded readiness criteria for product design, process capability, equipment, tooling, fixtures, test, materials, repair, capacity, and supplier controls. Lead critical builds, make evidence-based go/no-go recommendations, and drive recovery when product or process maturity does not meet the required manufacturing bar.
Factory Operations and Capacity Readiness : Assess and develop production-line capability, factory layouts, staffing models, equipment plans, tooling, fixtures, test coverage, material readiness, repair operations, and capacity models. Identify gaps before build start and lead cross-functional recovery actions to protect schedule, quality, capacity, and supply continuity. Provide direct technical leadership during critical factory builds and production excursions.
Supplier Management and Production Risk Mitigation : Provide technical leadership to contract manufacturers, ODMs, OEMs, component suppliers, and sub-tier partners. Assess manufacturing capability, process maturity, qualification status, compliance, capacity, interoperability, and business-continuity risks. Influence supplier investment and corrective actions while aligning sourcing, supply chain, engineering, and program stakeholders.
Manufacturing Process and Supplier Readiness : Lead supplier process qualification and readiness assessments, including process audits, PPAP activities, control plans, fixture and tooling acceptance, incoming-quality criteria, line validation, test coverage, and repair readiness. Develop and standardize manufacturing processes that enable repeatable production, measurable yield improvement, and scalable ramp across global manufacturing sites.
Quality Systems and Process Control : Apply statistical process control, process-capability analysis, measurement-system analysis, control plans, inspection data, and yield analytics to reduce variation and detect defects early. Drive practical automation, digital monitoring, vision inspection, AI-enabled analytics, and factory-data improvements where they provide measurable quality, efficiency, or operational value.
Root Cause Analysis and Continuous Improvement : Lead complex manufacturing issue triage and structured problem-solving using methods such as 8D, fishbone, 5-Why, PFMEA, DFMEA, and Six Sigma. Establish containment, isolate root cause, verify corrective-action effectiveness, prevent recurrence, and capture reusable lessons across products, suppliers, factories, and programs.
Technical Validation and Risk Management : Own manufacturing risk identification and mitigation across NUDD, PFMEA, qualification, yield, tooling, materials, supplier readiness, schedule, and capacity. Lead engineering-change impact assessments, tolerance analyses, simulations, failure-mode evaluations, and technical trade-offs. Escalate risks with clear options, supporting data, business impact, and actionable recommendations.
Metrics, Governance, and Executive Communication : Establish dashboards and operating mechanisms for build readiness, qualification, yield, defect trends, issue aging, risk closure, supplier performance, capacity, and corrective actions. Convert detailed manufacturing data into concise technical and business narratives that enable timely decisions by engineering, program, and executive leadership.
Cross-Program Strategy and Knowledge Transfer : Identify common manufacturing challenges across product generations and develop reusable standards, roadmaps, supplier strategies, qualification methods, and process improvements. Transfer lessons learned across products, suppliers, and factories; mentor engineers; strengthen the technical capability of the broader virtual team; and create clarity and accountability in ambiguous execution environments.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
Master's Degree in Manufacturing, Material, Mechanical, Electrical, Thermal, or Industrial Engineering, or related field AND 4+ years experience in a manufacturing environment /repair OR Bachelor's Degree in Manufacturing, Material, Mechanical, Electrical, Thermal, or Industrial Engineering, or related field AND 5+ years experience in a manufacturing environment/repair OR equivalent experience.
Other Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:  Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud Background Check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.
Preferred Qualifications:
Doctorate in Manufacturing, Material, Mechanical, Electrical, Thermal, or Industrial Engineering, or related field AND 3+ years experience in a manufacturing environment/repair OR Master's Degree in Manufacturing, Material, Mechanical, Electrical, Thermal, or Industrial Engineering, or related field AND 6+ years experience in a manufacturing environment/repair OR Bachelor's Degree in Manufacturing, Material, Mechanical, Electrical, Thermal, or Industrial Engineering, or related field AND 8+ years experience in a manufacturing environment/repair OR equivalent experience. Patent or track record of engineering excellency.
Strong leadership, facilitation, communication, problem-solving, and L1/L2 triage skills, with proven effectiveness across all organizational levels.
Ability to prioritize and execute in high-pressure, fast-paced environments while independently driving complex manufacturing challenges to resolution.
Deep hardware manufacturing expertise spanning assembly, test, tooling, fixtures, process qualification, factory operations, quality systems, repair, and production ramp.
Experience leading manufacturing engineering for AI, GPU, HPC, or rack-scale systems involving optical networking, high-speed interconnects, custom silicon, and disaggregated architectures.
Hands-on experience developing, qualifying, and manufacturing optical and high-speed connectivity components, including transceivers, cables, fiber assemblies, connectors, and related technologies.
Expertise in NPI and defining factory test, qualification, and reliability strategies for high-speed electrical and optical systems, including bring-up, interoperability, telemetry, fault isolation, and configuration control.
Proven ability to influence product architecture and design through DFM, testability, process capability, risk management, manufacturing trade-offs, and engineering change assessments.
Experience leading NPI, production ramp, and supplier ecosystems across globally distributed teams, ODMs/OEMs, contract manufacturers, system integrators, and sub-tier suppliers.
Strong track record applying data-driven manufacturing methodologies (SPC, PFMEA, 8D, Six Sigma, yield analytics, MSA, control plans), driving scalable improvements, translating technical data into executive recommendations, and utilizing PLM/MES/project-tracking tools, must meet security-screening requirements, if any.

title: Technical Program Manager II- Readiness Assessment & OEM Quality
description:
Overview
Microsoft's Windows Ecosystem and Commercial Engagement organization is building a closed-loop quality-readiness system for strategically important third-party OEM devices. The system connects OEM and silicon readiness, structured Readiness Assessment, controlled entrance into SelfHost, launch decisions, and post-launch learning. Its purpose is not to produce more activity or another dashboard. It is to give leaders and partners a trustworthy answer to whether a hardware-software configuration is ready to advance, what evidence supports that call, what risk remains, and who owns the next action.
As a Technical Program Manager II , you will own the program mechanisms surrounding this system: portfolio intake, partner alignment, integrated planning, readiness governance, risk and dependency management, decision records, and executive communication. You will work across Hero Device Engineering (HDE) and Hero Device Validation (HDV) program teams, OEM and silicon partners, Windows engineering, lab and test leads, data and reporting teams, SelfHost operations, and internal marketing and sales. You will turn ambiguity into an operating model and technical evidence into decisions while protecting partner trust and clear engineering accountability.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Lead the end-to-end program operating model for a portfolio of strategic OEM device readiness initiatives, from portfolio intake and scenario definition through OEM self-assessment, Microsoft Readiness Assessment, SelfHost entrance, release milestones, and post-launch learning.
Build and maintain integrated plans that connect OEM and silicon schedules, device availability, hardware and software manifests, BIOS, firmware, drivers, images, lab capacity, assessment criteria, evidence requirements, remediation work, and decision gates.
Create trusted partnerships with HDE and HDV program managers, OEM counterparts, silicon partners, engineering and quality teams, internal marketing and sales, and senior leaders. Clarify roles, service expectations, handoffs, decision rights, and escalation paths across organizational boundaries.
Drive portfolio prioritization using customer personas, product and sales importance, reviewer influence, new silicon or architecture risk, technical novelty, historical escapes, and available capacity. Make tradeoffs visible and recommend where impartial Microsoft evidence matters most.
This role requires the confidence to manage requests and weigh the resource capacity, schedule implications, and ROI. Ensuring clear outcomes, owners, capacity plan, or approved tradeoffs.
Establish and run scalable governance, including weekly portfolio reviews, milestone and readiness reviews, integrated risk and dependency tracking, gate-exception records, and decision logs. Ensure every material risk has an accountable owner, next action, date, closure evidence, and escalation path.
Facilitate readiness and entrance decisions using defined criteria, evidence confidence, hard-stop conditions, and explicit exceptions. Record the decision authority, rationale, residual risk, and evidence that would change the posture; never allow schedule pressure or incomplete data to become a silent gate bypass.
Translate assessment findings, telemetry, quality signals, and partner status into concise, decision-ready recommendations for technical and executive audiences. Separate measured facts from targets and estimates, surface unknowns and data-quality limitations, and communicate what needs to happen next.
Drive timely issue routing and follow-through across OEM, silicon, Windows, tooling, and operational owners. You will not own every technical fix, but you will make ownership gaps, aging dependencies, unresolved tradeoffs, and decisions requiring leadership action impossible to miss.
Define and improve portfolio metrics such as on-time verdicts, critical-criteria coverage, evidence completeness, receipt-to-verdict time, partner response aging, owner and disposition timeliness, capacity returned through automation, and covered post-launch escapes. Partner with data owners to preserve definitions, provenance, and confidence.
Scale the system through reusable intake contracts, templates, playbooks, service-level expectations, retrospectives, and AI-assisted workflows. Partner with lab and engineering leads on test automation and OEM self-assessment  while retaining deterministic validation, accountable human judgment, Microsoft audit authority, and OEM confidentiality.

1+ year(s) of experience managing cross-functional and/or cross-team projects.
Preferred Qualifications:

2+ years of experience managing cross-functional or cross-team projects with interdependent technical, operational, partner, and business deliverables.
Experience gathering business and technical requirements and translating them into program plans, milestones, readiness criteria, decision gates, metrics, and accountable actions.
Demonstrated experience using data to assess program health, identify and mitigate risks, manage dependencies, resolve ambiguity, and influence technical and business decisions.
Demonstrated ability to communicate complex technical and program information clearly to engineers, partner organizations, business stakeholders, and senior leaders, and to drive alignment without direct authority.

PMP, PgMP, Lean, Six Sigma, Agile, or comparable program-management training or demonstrated practical mastery of those disciplines.

description:
About the Team

The Product Policy research team studies how people use and experience AI, generating evidence to inform product, policy, and safety decisions. We partner with researchers, data scientists, engineers, and cross-functional teams to understand AI’s effects on people’s lives, including well-being, youth experiences, and social and emotional use.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Applied Scientist to help design, execute, and analyze large-scale longitudinal research on AI use and well-being. You’ll work closely with research leads to translate scientific questions into rigorous studies, combining survey responses with behavioral data to understand how people’s experiences with AI evolve over time.

This is a hands-on role spanning applied analysis, research methods, and study execution. You’ll build reproducible analytical workflows, assess data quality and representativeness, and help establish reliable infrastructure for ongoing panel research. Your work will support research involving teens and adults, including studies of AI companionship, and help turn findings into useful evidence for product, policy, and safety partners.

In this role, you will:

 - Partner with research leads to develop study designs, survey measures, and analysis plans for longitudinal research on AI use and well-being.

 - Conduct statistical analyses of survey and behavioral data, including evaluating selection and response bias, account-linkage patterns, and sample representativeness.

 - Prepare and validate analysis-ready datasets, implement analysis plans, and produce clear summaries and visualizations using reproducible workflows.

 - Develop quality checks across survey programming, fieldwork, data delivery, and repeated study waves to identify inconsistencies and improve research reliability.

 - Own day-to-day study execution, coordinating timelines, vendors, and cross-functional dependencies to deliver high-quality research on schedule.

 - Collaborate with data engineering and privacy partners on responsible account linkage, data flows, logging, and retention.

 - Maintain clear documentation of methods, measures, assumptions, and protocol changes, and contribute analysis and methodological materials for research readouts, publications, and peer review.

 - Communicate findings, limitations, and practical recommendations to technical and nontechnical partners, and build reusable tools and processes that improve future studies.

 - Bring strong foundations in survey research and statistical analysis, with experience working on panel studies, longitudinal datasets, or human-subjects research.

 - Are comfortable using SQL and Python or R to prepare data, implement analyses, validate results, and create visualizations.

 - Understand how recruitment, missing data, participant attrition, and measurement choices can affect the interpretation and generalizability of findings.

 - Can move between analytical work and practical execution, managing multiple timelines and collaborators while maintaining scientific rigor.

title: Compute Electrical Engineer, Robotics
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and advancing toward AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world environments. Working across the full model and systems stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the physical constraints of real-world systems to improve people’s lives.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an Electrical Engineer to develop the AI inference compute systems that power OpenAI’s humanoid robots. This role combines compute architecture, high-speed digital design, onboard power electronics, and compact HDI PCB development.

We’re looking for a self-driven engineer who takes ownership from concept through deployment. Above all, you should enjoy hands-on engineering: bringing up boards, characterizing interfaces, and tracking challenging failures to their root cause.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own compute hardware architecture and development, from component selection and schematic design through PCB layout, validation, and deployment.

 - Design and integrate high-speed interfaces—including PCIe, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, USB, and DisplayPort—balancing bandwidth, connectivity, power, and signal integrity.

 - Develop onboard DC-to-DC conversion and power distribution to meet efficiency, transient-response, sequencing, and power-integrity requirements.

 - Define HDI PCB stackups, dielectric materials, via structures, and routing strategies that balance electrical performance, manufacturability, reliability, and cost.

 - Lead bench bring-up and validation, including test planning, high-speed interface characterization, power measurements, and debugging through verified resolution.

 - Partner with thermal, mechanical, EMC, and software teams to integrate compute hardware into tightly constrained robotic systems.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have 5+ years of experience developing compute hardware or similarly complex high-speed electronics, with demonstrated ownership of complete designs.

 - Bring strong hands-on measurement and debugging skills, including practical experience with oscilloscopes, probing techniques, and interface validation.

Working directly with the Head of Creative, Business, you will lead resource planning and allocation across our internal creative team, contractors, and agency partners—balancing ongoing campaigns with rapidly emerging launches and requests.

You’ll develop a deep understanding of our creative talent and capabilities, translate business priorities into thoughtful staffing plans, and help teams navigate competing demands without sacrificing craft or quality. title: Electrical Engineer, PCBA Test Infrastructure, Robotics
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking an Electrical Engineer for a senior individual-contributor role leading printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) test infrastructure for advanced robotic systems. You will independently turn evolving requirements into working test stations, make technical tradeoffs, and own delivery from architecture and circuit design through validation, deployment, and reliable operation.

This role combines development-lab work with deployment at contract manufacturers. You will develop electrical test systems for board bring-up, programming, functional test, and characterization, partnering with mechanical, firmware, software, manufacturing, and reliability teams to carry validated stations from prototypes into repeat builds.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 4 days a week. Travel to contract-manufacturer sites is part of the role, with timing based on build and deployment needs.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own PCBA test-station architecture, including device-under-test interfaces, programmable power, electronic loads, signal routing, instrumentation, and protection.

 - Translate board requirements and likely failure modes into test coverage, measurement methods, and pass/fail criteria. Partner with board designers on design for test, test-point access, programming interfaces, and diagnostics.

 - Design and bring up fixture interface boards, switching circuits, harnesses, and connectors. Release schematics, PCB layouts, wiring diagrams, bills of materials, and interface definitions.

 - Integrate oscilloscopes, meters, power supplies, loads, and data acquisition hardware; validate calibration, timing, accuracy, and repeatability across stations and board revisions.

 - Develop and debug programming and communications interfaces such as JTAG/SWD, UART, SPI, I²C, CAN, and Ethernet as required by the board. Diagnose power, signal-integrity, grounding, and contact problems.

 - Design and validate current limiting, power sequencing, ESD protection, interlocks, and fault recovery appropriate to the hardware under test.

 - Partner with mechanical engineers on probe access, connector mating, board support, cooling, and serviceability. Work with firmware and software partners to define interfaces and integrate test stations with shared software.

 - Write, debug, and maintain test code for instrument control, board programming, automated sequences, diagnostics, and result logging. Collaborate with software partners on reusable frameworks, code reviews, and reliable releases.

 - Establish station commissioning, calibration, maintenance, and configuration control. Track board identity and revision, firmware version, test limits, and station configuration with each result.

 - Use reference boards, independent measurements, and deliberate fault checks to distinguish board failures from fixture or software errors. Improve test coverage, false-failure rate, cycle time, and station uptime.

 - Own test-station deployment and acceptance at contract manufacturers, including station correlation, build support, operator training, and troubleshooting. Release configurations and documentation that keep lab and factory results consistent.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have strong intuition for analog and digital circuits, power delivery, electronics debugging, and reliable measurement.

 - Move comfortably from architecture and circuit design to soldering, probing, scripting, and troubleshooting in the lab.

 - Care about grounding, shielding, contact quality, calibration, and evidence that a test detects the faults it is intended to find.

 - Take ownership from prototype through reliable daily operation, balancing rapid iteration with clear documentation and maintainable test systems.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Demonstrated ability to independently deliver significant electronics test-system projects from ambiguous requirements through working hardware, validation, and sustained use.

 - Hands-on capability in circuit and fixture-interface design, schematic interpretation, board bring-up, power delivery, signal switching, and instrument integration.

 - Ability to independently debug PCBAs and test hardware using oscilloscopes, meters, logic analyzers, and systematic root-cause investigation.

 - Ability to write, debug, and maintain code that interfaces with real hardware in Python or a comparable language, including instrument control, sequencing, error handling, and structured result logging.

 - Practical understanding of grounding, signal integrity, calibration, measurement uncertainty, ESD controls, power sequencing, and electrical protection.

 - Ability to release clear test and hardware documentation, coordinate across engineering disciplines, and support hands-on deployment and troubleshooting at contract manufacturers.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - Prior PCBA functional-test or automated-test-equipment experience, including design for test, test coverage, fixture correlation, and new-product builds at contract manufacturers.

 - Experience with embedded programming, diagnostic firmware, and board interfaces such as JTAG/SWD, UART, SPI, I²C, CAN, or Ethernet.

 - Experience with PCB design tools, shared test-automation frameworks, production data systems, or robotics hardware.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Commission a reusable PCBA test station with documented coverage, acceptance criteria, and traceable results; deploy and validate a reproducible configuration at a contract manufacturer.

 - Demonstrate measurement repeatability and intended fault detection using reference boards, independent measurements, and known-fault cases. Track false failures, cycle time, and uptime against agreed improvement targets.

 - Release hardware documentation, versioned test code, commissioning checks, and troubleshooting procedures that enable lab and contract-manufacturer teams to reproduce, operate, and maintain the station

The Candidate Experience team ensures that every interaction candidates and interviewers have with OpenAI reflects excellence, fairness, and humanity. This team owns global coordination, interview logistics, onsite experience, Interview Programs, and the operational workflows that support all recruiting functions, from Executive and Research to Technical, GTM, and G&A. As OpenAI scales globally, this team plays a critical role in designing experiences that are both bespoke for highly specialized searches and scalable across rapidly growing teams and offices.

About the Role

As Global Candidate Experience Manager, you will manage CE managers and Interview Programs program managers, with global responsibility for candidate experience, coordination and interview program delivery. You will lead through the team’s managers, leads and program owners while staying close enough to daily work to understand where it breaks. You will own service quality, capacity planning, interviewer readiness, program delivery and continuous improvement across high-volume and highly bespoke hiring.

As part of our expanding Data Science function, we’re building a best-in-class Forecasting capability to drive real-time, data-driven decision-making across user growth, revenue, compute infrastructure, and more.

 

We are developing scalable forecasting infrastructure to help us understand and anticipate business dynamics in an increasingly complex, usage-based world. Our models are foundational to planning, pricing, operational efficiency, and growth strategy - supporting key investment decisions and unlocking OpenAI’s full potential.

 

About the Role

We’re looking for a senior Machine Learning Data Scientist to lead our forecasting initiatives. You’ll be one of the founding members of the Forecasting pillar within Strategic Finance Data Science, responsible for building and scaling robust, interpretable, and production-ready forecasting systems. Your models will power critical business decisions by predicting core metrics such as DAU/WAU, revenue, LTV, compute consumption, and profitability.

 

This is a highly cross-functional role, requiring technical excellence, strong product intuition, and business acumen. You’ll collaborate with product managers, researchers, engineers, and finance leaders to operationalize forecasting insights, influence company-wide strategy, and build foundational forecasting capabilities at OpenAI.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 

In this role, you will:

 - Build statistical and machine learning models to solve forecasting needs across product, finance, infrastructure, and GTM domains.

 - Own the end-to-end modeling lifecycle, including scoping, feature engineering, model development and prototyping, experimentation, deployment, monitoring, and explainability.

 - Develop and productionize scalable, interpretable forecasts for user growth, monetization, compute load, customer lifetime value, and profitability.

 - Contribute to self-service forecasting tools and internal platforms, enabling teams across OpenAI to access and act on real-time predictions.

 - Research and evaluate emerging tools and techniques in the forecasting space, such as TimeGPT, large language model extensions, causal forecasting, and hybrid approaches.

 - Drive strategic insight generation by translating technical outputs into business-aligned recommendations and decision frameworks.

 - Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to ensure forecasts are well-integrated into planning processes, experimentation workflows, and executive decision-making.





You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - Advanced degree (MS or PhD) in a quantitative field (e.g., Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, Operations Research).

 - 7+ years of experience in applied data science, with deep hands-on exposure to forecasting, predictive modeling, or marketplace systems.

 - Expertise in time-series forecasting techniques and practical understanding of model trade-offs across performance, explainability, and scalability.

 - Proficiency in Python, SQL, and tools such as scikit-learn, PyTorch/TensorFlow, and forecasting libraries.

 - Strong communication and storytelling skills - able to simplify complexity and influence executive stakeholders.

 - Self-directed, intellectually curious, and comfortable leading ambiguous projects from 0→1.

 - Experience building or scaling forecasting platforms in a high-growth company.

 - Experience building agentic decision support systems.

title: Mechanical Engineer, PCBA Test Infrastructure, Robotics
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a Mechanical Engineer for a senior individual-contributor role leading printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) test fixtures and infrastructure for advanced robotic systems. You will independently turn evolving requirements into working fixtures, make technical tradeoffs, and own delivery from concept and detailed design through fabrication, validation, deployment, and reliable operation.

This role combines development-lab work with deployment at contract manufacturers. You will build precision mechanical systems for board programming, functional test, and characterization, including board nests, probe plates, connector interfaces, alignment features, clamps, enclosures, and thermal interfaces. You will partner with electrical, firmware, software, manufacturing, and reliability teams to make fixtures repeatable, protective of delicate assemblies, and maintainable as board designs evolve.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 4 days a week. Travel to contract-manufacturer sites is part of the role, with timing based on build and deployment needs.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own the mechanical architecture of PCBA test stations, including frames, board nests, datum schemes, access, guarding, ergonomics, and serviceability.

 - Design probe and bed-of-nails fixtures, connector-mating mechanisms, board supports, clamps, and interchangeable tooling for programming, functional test, and characterization.

 - Use first-principles analysis and simulation to assess stiffness, probe and insertion forces, board deflection, tolerance stacks, thermal growth, and fixture life; validate key predictions on hardware.

 - Develop locating and compliance features that accommodate board and assembly variation, protect components and solder joints, and preserve contact repeatability across loading cycles and board revisions.

 - Partner with electrical engineers on test-point access, probe selection, connector engagement, ESD provisions, cable routing, cooling, and interlocks; define motion and sequencing constraints with software and controls partners.

 - Build, assemble, instrument, and debug fixtures in the lab. Establish acceptance checks for alignment, force, board strain where needed, contact repeatability, and cycle life; separate fixture problems from board failures.

 - Design safe loading, pinch-point protection, hard stops, and operator access for manual or actuated fixtures. Make wear components easy to inspect, clean, and replace.

 - Manage fabrication partners and component vendors. Release CAD, drawings, bills of materials, tolerance analyses, assembly instructions, inspection plans, and maintenance procedures.

 - Own fixture deployment and acceptance at contract manufacturers, including assembly and alignment checks, correlation with lab fixtures, operator training, and troubleshooting. Support replication, board-revision changes, and maintenance through released documentation.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have strong mechanical intuition for precision interfaces, load paths, compliance, tolerances, and the behavior of delicate electronic assemblies.

 - Move readily between analysis, CAD, vendor collaboration, and hands-on assembly and debugging.

 - Care about repeatable contact, controlled forces, operator usability, and equipment that others can maintain.

 - Take ownership from concept through reliable daily operation, adapting fixtures to evolving boards and communicating clearly across electrical, software, manufacturing, and operations teams.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Demonstrated ability to independently deliver significant precision-fixture or equipment projects from ambiguous requirements through detailed design, fabrication, validation, and sustained use.

 - Strong 3D CAD and released-drawing capability, including complete fabrication and assembly packages, bills of materials, and revision control.

 - Strong fundamentals in GD&T, tolerance analysis, locating schemes, stiffness, compliance, contact forces, and load paths.

 - Hands-on ability to work with fabrication partners, assemble and measure fixtures, diagnose failures, and iterate hardware in a lab or manufacturing environment.

 - Ability to define and execute fixture acceptance checks for alignment, force, repeatability, wear, and safe operation, using evidence to distinguish fixture problems from product variation.

 - Ability to communicate interfaces and tradeoffs across electrical, software, manufacturing, and operations teams and support deployment and troubleshooting at contract manufacturers.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - Prior PCBA test-fixture experience with board nests, probe or bed-of-nails fixtures, connector mating, and protection of delicate electronic assemblies.

 - Experience with ESD-aware tooling, thermal interfaces, actuated fixtures, interlocks, or structural and thermal simulation.

 - Experience with NX, SolidWorks, Creo, or equivalent tools; robotics hardware; or fixture replication and new-product builds at contract manufacturers.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Deliver a reusable PCBA fixture that meets agreed alignment, contact, board-support, and loading requirements, with demonstrated repeatability and protection of the assembly under test.

 - Validate fixture wear and cycle life, identify sources of intermittent contact or board loading, and improve contact-related failures, changeover time, and serviceability against agreed targets.

 - Deploy and accept the fixture at a contract manufacturer with released CAD, drawings, inspection checks, assembly instructions, spare-parts information, and maintenance procedures that enable others to reproduce and sustain it.

title: Product Reliability Engineer
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops silicon and system-level solutions designed for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. The team is responsible for building the next generation of AI-native silicon while working closely with software and research partners to co-design hardware tightly integrated with AI models. In addition to delivering production-grade silicon for OpenAI’s supercomputing infrastructure, the team also creates custom design tools and methodologies that accelerate innovation and enable hardware optimized specifically for AI.

The Compute team works on the design of our AI supercomputers, doing everything from workload modeling to influencing accelerator design. We’re leaning into our partnerships to make system and data center co-design an integral part of this process, and are looking for engineers to design AI supercomputers solutions for data center applications

This team is responsible for working with partners to optimize their hardware for our workloads, identifying promising new deep learning accelerators, and bringing those hardware platforms to production.

If you’re excited to work at the intersection of cutting edge deep learning, hardware system, and data center design this role is for you!

About the Role

We’re looking for a Product Reliability Engineer to own reliability engineering for advanced IT hardware, from printed circuit board assemblies (PCBAs) through compute and networking trays, systems, and fully integrated racks. You’ll translate operating conditions and service-life goals into reliability requirements, design and execute qualification tests, and drive failure analysis and corrective-action verification from development through production and field deployment. Working with electrical, mechanical, thermal, manufacturing, quality, and data center teams, suppliers, and manufacturing partners, you’ll use test and field evidence to improve hardware durability, serviceability, and availability.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Define reliability requirements and targets for PCBAs, trays, systems, and racks using mission profiles, expected service life, operating environments, duty cycles, and availability goals.

 - Drive design-for-reliability reviews with electrical, mechanical, and thermal engineers. Use failure modes and effects analysis (DFMEA or FMEA) and physics of failure to prioritize risks and recommend design improvements. Own component de-rating guidelines and guidance.

 - Own reliability qualification plans from new product introduction through production, defining test coverage, representative configurations, sample sizes, stress conditions, duration, pass/fail criteria, and exit evidence at each assembly level.

 - Develop and execute accelerated life and environmental tests, including temperature cycling, humidity exposure, power cycling, shock, vibration, and transport testing. Exercise hardware under representative workloads and monitor function and degradation during stress.

 - Analyze life-test and field data using Weibull and other reliability models, acceleration models, and confidence intervals. State assumptions, exposure, and uncertainty when estimating failure rates, useful life, or reliability against targets.

 - Lead failure investigations from symptom reproduction through physical root cause. Maintain failure reporting, analysis, and corrective-action records, and verify fixes through targeted testing and recurrence monitoring.

 - Review supplier reliability plans and evidence for PCBs, PCBa components/assemblies, cables, connectors, and cooling components. Identify gaps between component qualification and the stresses encountered in the integrated system or rack.

 - Work hands-on with internal and partner labs to develop fixtures, instrumentation, and test methods. Review sample traceability, test configurations, calibration, raw data, and failure capture, including on-site support at manufacturing partners.

 - Partner with manufacturing and quality engineers to establish and validate reliability screens, burn-in where justified, and ongoing reliability testing. Confirm screening detects relevant defects without consuming unacceptable product life.

 - Evaluate reliability risks introduced by assembly and integration: board strain and solder-joint damage, connector mating and retention, cable routing, fastener preload, power connections, and thermal interfaces. Partner with cooling specialists on leak integrity, material compatibility, corrosion, and cooling performance over life.

 - Plan reliability test resources, lab capacity, hardware samples, schedules, and dependencies across programs with engineering teams, technical program managers, suppliers, and manufacturing partners.

 - Present qualification results, unresolved failure modes, and residual risk at design and release reviews. Make evidence-based readiness recommendations and clearly identify test gaps, required follow-up, and decisions for accountable owners.

 - Assess reliability impact and define targeted requalification for design, component, supplier, manufacturing process, and repair changes, including firmware changes that alter hardware operating stresses.

 - Track field returns and fleet failure trends with service and data center teams. Correlate telemetry, failure analysis, and configuration history to prioritize corrective actions and feed lessons into future designs and qualification plans.

 - Validate serviceability and repeated assembly or maintenance operations, including connector mating cycles and component replacement. Work with system engineers to assess how hardware failures, redundancy, and recovery affect rack availability.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have hands-on reliability engineering experience with advanced IT hardware, such as AI/HPC servers, networking equipment, or storage systems, spanning PCBAs, electromechanical assemblies, and integrated racks.

 - Have designed, instrumented, and executed hardware reliability tests, debugged failures in the lab, and translated results into practical design or process improvements.

 - Understand failure mechanisms in electronic assemblies, including solder fatigue, PCB and laminate damage, connector wear, corrosion, and thermal or mechanical degradation.

 - Can turn mission profiles and failure risks into qualification plans, select defensible sample sizes and stress levels, and explain the assumptions and limits of accelerated testing.

 - Have led reliability qualification through development and production milestones, balancing sample availability, lab capacity, schedule, and the evidence needed for release decisions.

 - Have worked directly with component suppliers, joint design manufacturers, contract manufacturers, and external test labs to review test methods, resolve failures, and verify corrective actions.

 - Apply design for reliability, DFMEA, and physics-of-failure methods across electrical, mechanical, and thermal interfaces, and understand how manufacturing, assembly, handling, and repair affect long-term reliability.

 - Have driven structured failure analysis and corrective action using methods such as 8D, supported by electrical diagnostics, microscopy, X-ray, cross-section analysis, or specialist failure-analysis labs as appropriate.

 - Can analyze reliability and life-test data, including censored data, Weibull distributions, and confidence bounds, using tools such as Python, R, JMP, or equivalent statistical software.

 - Bring experience with high-power electronics, dense interconnects, or liquid-cooled hardware, including thermal interfaces, leak integrity, material compatibility, and serviceability.

 - Communicate technical findings and uncertainty clearly, distinguish verified root cause and corrective-action effectiveness from hypotheses, and prioritize reliability risks when requirements or designs change.

title: Software Engineer II - Growth
description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE ROLE
Software Engineer II, Growth
We are seeking a Software Engineer II for the Growth Marketing Engineering Team. You are the kind of engineer who gravitates toward the hardest problems at the intersection of technology and performance marketing: designing a low-latency bidding optimization engine, building a reliable creative generation pipeline, or defining the architectural patterns that will shape how Quince scales its growth stack. You operate with high autonomy, hold yourself to exceptional standards, and naturally raise the bar for the engineers around you through rigorous code reviews, sharp technical judgment, and a bias toward clean, durable solutions over quick fixes.
Responsibilities
Designing and implementing software features and components, following best practices and coding standards with minimal supervision.
Contributing to identifying the root cause of complex problems, scale, and stability challenges.
Proposing a solution to mitigate them in the short/medium/long term horizon.
Keeping up-to-date with new technologies, frameworks, and best practices in software development, and applying them to improve the performance and reliability of software systems.
Writing and maintaining technical documentation, API specifications, code documentation, and technical design documents.
Participating in code reviews and contributing to the development of coding standards and best practices.
Mentoring junior engineers and contributing to their professional growth and development.
Leading software development projects and working collaboratively with cross-functional teams to deliver high-quality software products
Qualifications
Required
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science or a related field.
At least 2 years of professional experience working in building user facing products.
Experience in advertisement performance tooling is a plus.
Proficient in using debugging tools and techniques.
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
Ability to work independently as well as part of a team.
Understand the hustle of a startup and are good with handling ambiguity.
Effectively communicate with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Curious, quick learner, scrappy and someone who loves to experiment.

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

Proactively manage supply chain risks, including single-source dependencies and long-lead-time components, by executing robust mitigation plans and Risk Buy decisions. Partner with Engineering on component lifecycle stability, obsolescence management, and End-of-Life (EOL) planning. Closely work with the supplier and cross-functional teams to gauge the need for PPVs and complete the supply chain risk analysis as needed. Operational & Stakeholder Management Collaborate cross-functionally to provide detailed forecasting and cost data, supporting long-term vehicle program planning. Optimize inventory levels at Contract Manufacturers to minimize Excess and Obsolete (E&O) material while maximizing financial efficiency. Build and maintain strong relationships with Tier 1 suppliers, monitoring performance against key supply chain and quality metrics. Proactively identify and implement supply chain system improvements to drive procurement speed and accuracy. Supplier & Commercial Management: Minimum 3+ years of relevant experience managing technical and commercial business relationships with large suppliers in an Automotive, Electronics, or high-volume manufacturing business. Lifecycle Management: Demonstrated expertise in managing materials across the entire product lifecycle: Quick Turn, NPI, and Mass Production. Join Our Team as a Mold Machine Operator!
S&C Electric Company is seeking a dynamic individual to coordinate our  Mold machining  function. As a  Mold machinist , you’ll be crucial in ensuring smooth operations and supporting our diverse team. A Mold Machine Operator is responsible for operating an injection molding machine to produce polymer components efficiently. This role involves reviewing job orders and blueprints, setting up molds, adjusting parameters, and monitoring production to maintain optimal machinery conditions.
Key Responsibilities:
Operate injection molding machine, ensuring the smooth and efficient production of simple polymer components.
Review job orders and simple blueprints to understand molding requirements.
Set up molds, adjust parameters, and monitor production, maintaining optimal operating conditions for the machinery.
Comfortable wearing respirator for different periods of time.
Cycle molding machine and monitor its progress while performing secondary operations such as deflashing, inspection, visual and mechanical application of lubricating grease, and packaging of finished product.
Inspect finished products for defects, following quality assurance guidelines and escalating quality issues when needed.
Use hand tools like files, hammer, scrapper, air nozzle to blow off excess and clean molds, maintaining cleanliness and functionality of equipment.
Apply silicone mold release with a brush to ensure things don’t stick, facilitating efficient production processes.
Perform sandblasting operations as required.
Document completed jobs, ensuring accuracy and prompt reporting of issues.
Meet department targets and consistently adhere to quality and safety standards.
Understand and comply with all applicable Company policies and rules.
Work with departmental mentors to gain and apply feedback in pursuit of improved work quality.
Maintain regular and punctual attendance.
Attend in-person or virtual meetings as requested or required.
Communicate effectively and respectfully with others.
Other responsibilities as assigned.

High School Diploma or Equivalent Experience.
Entry level experience in a production environment.
Ability to use hand tools.
Basic knowledge of machine controls and programs.
Ability to work independently and meet requirements of assigned materials requests.
Good communication skills (written and verbal) with the ability to articulate information efficiently and effectively to team members in a variety of production support departments. Able to escalate and explain issues to team leads and supervisors as needed.
Basic computer skills with the ability to review and respond to requests via internal applications.
Basic math skills with the ability to calculate quantities, weights, and measurements.
Good interpersonal and organizational skills with the ability to understand and complete requests given by team members inside and outside of the department.
Good critical thinking skills with the ability to solve problems and understand efforts to improve processes.
Good attention to detail with the ability to complete precise tasks and follow instructions accurately.
Ability and willingness to follow Health Safety & Environment procedures accurately, reporting concerns promptly to the safety action team.

description:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role:
This is a dynamic, high energy role in which you will bring the Internet of Things to mid-sized customers, building Samsara's business and bringing the benefits of sensor data to customers. Typical sales will be $20k to $100k, and involve POCs, multiple stakeholders, managing trials, multi-faceted pricing negotiations, and selling to executives and CXOs.
This role is open for candidates residing in the following US states: North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, Ohio, Indiana, Illinois, Iowa. The role requires travel approximately 25% of the time.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
Your mantra is #alwaysbeprospecting: The world of operations is vast. Your customers are often out in the field and the best way to catch them is live on the phone. Samsara’s top reps do constant research to find companies and contacts to expand their pipeline.
You have innate curiosity in how businesses work: One day you’ll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.
You are a life-long learner: Samsara sales are complex. You will need to learn about businesses where you previously had little knowledge. The payoff is big but you have to be willing to put in the work.
You build genuine relationships with your customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven’t been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.
You want to be with the best: Samsara’s high-performance Sales culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.
Minimum requirements for this role:
2+ years experience in a full-cycle, closing sales role
Experience independently closing new deals larger than $10,000 in annual revenue
All candidates must be located in one of the following states: North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, Ohio, Indiana, Illinois, Iowa.
An ideal candidate has:
Proven track record of consistent quota achievement
Experience selling in the midmarket space - medium to large deals sizes
Experience with high-volume cold calling
Must demonstrate a growth mindset and a willingness to be collaborative with your teammates and in your selling process
SFDC familiarity

We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.
Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.
Flexible Working
At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.
Belonging at Samsara
At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.
Accommodations
Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email accessibleinterviewing@samsara.com or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.
